title: After hours intrusion
Outcome: Detect people in a protected area while its security schedule is armed and create a reviewable intrusion incident.
Inputs: Live video, person tracks, site timezone, zone geometry, opening schedule and temporary authorised-work windows.
Configure: Select Site > Rules > After hours; draw the protected polygon; choose days, holidays, entry grace seconds, minimum presence seconds and escalation recipients. Preview the armed calendar before publishing.
Journey: Administrator tests the zone with a recorded walk-through and activates the rule. > A person enters during an armed period; AiWAS records the qualifying interval and opens an alert with the rule explanation. > Operator opens the alert, checks live video and the before-and-after clip, then classifies the activity. > If confirmed, operator follows the site response procedure and assigns a guard; authorised work can be marked with an expiry. > Operator records the outcome and closes the incident; the client sees the verified summary.
Rules: Use event capture time for schedule evaluation. Start the dwell timer only inside the zone. Emit one incident per continuous track episode; do not repeatedly alert on every frame. Maintenance suppression must be time limited and audited.
Exceptions: Missing schedule blocks activation. Lost video changes coverage to unknown. Daylight-saving changes use the site's named timezone. A returning person creates a new episode only after the configured clear interval.
Acceptance: An armed-period entry beyond minimum presence creates one alert. An identical entry during opening hours creates none. A video gap produces a coverage fault rather than an all-clear. A holiday override follows its effective date.
Scope: Includes person presence and schedule rules. Excludes automatic identity inference and automatic police contact.
Dependencies: P01 tenancy; P02 video; P03 rules; P04 incident handling; F019 dispatch optional.
Outputs: Zone, person track, armed window, capture timestamps, evidence references, operator verdict and response outcome.

title: Virtual perimeter
Outcome: Detect directional crossings of a configured virtual boundary and distinguish entry from exit.
Inputs: Fixed-camera video, person or vehicle tracks, ordered line coordinates and optional protected-side polygon.
Configure: Draw a line, label inside and outside, choose object classes, crossing direction, minimum track age and cooldown. Display a test animation showing which movement will qualify.
Journey: Installer calibrates the camera and draws the boundary on the live preview. > Administrator runs crossing tests in both directions and publishes the accepted version. > AiWAS identifies a trajectory crossing from the unprotected to protected side and creates a boundary event. > Operator opens the event with the trajectory overlaid and verifies whether entry occurred. > Operator responds or dismisses with a reason, then reviews repeated false alerts with the installer.
Rules: Require track positions on both sides of the line; touching a line is insufficient. Apply the configured detection anchor consistently. Suppress oscillation around the line using hysteresis and an episode cooldown.
Exceptions: Tracks appearing on the protected side without a crossing are not crossing events; F003 can cover presence. Camera movement invalidates saved geometry until reviewed. Occlusion produces uncertain trajectories, not invented crossings.
Acceptance: Outside-to-inside movement triggers once. Inside-to-outside movement is ignored for an entry-only rule. Standing on the boundary does not repeatedly trigger. Repositioning the camera marks the rule for recalibration.
Scope: Includes geometric crossing. Excludes proving ownership, permission or criminal intent.
Dependencies: P02 video; P03 rules; F081 camera health.
Outputs: Crossing direction, line version, object class, trajectory and review clip.

title: Restricted zone entry
Outcome: Alert on presence in a controlled zone, including a person first detected already inside it.
Inputs: Camera stream, object tracks, zone polygon, armed schedule and optional access authorisations.
Configure: Name the protected asset or room; define inclusive and excluded regions; choose person or vehicle classes and minimum presence. Choose presence-only or authorisation-correlated operation.
Journey: Administrator selects the room and configures the zone and recipients. > Installer confirms the entire entry area is observable. > AiWAS detects sustained presence and attaches any available access grant. > Operator reviews the video and authorisation status before deciding whether entry is an exception. > Confirmed exceptions create a response task; allowed access is recorded with the supporting reference.
Rules: Presence-only mode labels the event zone entry, not unauthorised person. Authorisation-correlated mode requires a current matching grant and usable time alignment. Exclusion polygons take precedence over included zones.
Exceptions: An unavailable access system yields authorisation unknown. Camera blind spots remain visible in the commissioning record. Reflections and adjacent rooms must be excluded during setup.
Acceptance: A track first detected inside an armed zone qualifies after dwell. An object wholly in an excluded polygon does not qualify. An unavailable credential feed cannot silently approve entry.
Scope: Includes configured-zone monitoring and optional access context. Excludes identity recognition from clothing alone.
Dependencies: P03 rules; P04 incidents; P06 connectors; F024 access evidence optional.
Outputs: Zone occupancy event, rule reason, authorisation status and incident disposition.

title: Loitering near sensitive locations
Outcome: Surface prolonged presence near a sensitive location so an operator can assess the situation.
Inputs: Person or vehicle tracks, zone geometry, track continuity and active schedule.
Configure: Set dwell_seconds, allowed_gap_seconds, reset_after_exit_seconds, object classes and notification cooldown. Configure separate thresholds for each location rather than one global suspicion score.
Journey: Administrator draws the waiting area and selects a dwell threshold. > The preview shows how ordinary queues and staff work would be treated. > AiWAS accumulates qualifying dwell and displays elapsed duration when the threshold is reached. > Operator reviews activity, context and any previous related incident. > Operator offers assistance, intervenes or dismisses; false-positive reasons feed rule review.
Rules: Dwell describes visible presence, not intent. Brief validated tracking gaps may preserve the timer; uncertain identity breaks cannot be merged automatically. Separate multiple people and retain each qualifying interval.
Exceptions: A normal queue may require a schedule or exclusion. Occlusion beyond the gap limit resets continuity. Do not infer that a returning lookalike is the same person.
Acceptance: Presence just below threshold creates no alert. Crossing the threshold creates one episode. Leaving beyond reset time starts a fresh timer. A crowd does not inherit one person's dwell timer.
Scope: Includes time-in-area events. Excludes labelling someone dangerous or predicting an offence.
Dependencies: P03 rules; P04 incidents; F088 queue context optional.
Outputs: Observed dwell, confidence, interruptions, zone and review disposition.

title: Fence climbing detection
Outcome: Surface a possible person climbing over a visible physical fence for urgent verification.
Inputs: Time-sequenced video with sufficient fence and body visibility, fence geometry and a validated climbing model.
Configure: Mark the fence plane, top edge and both sides; select minimum sequence duration and an approved model profile. Require a successful scene-specific pilot before live alerts are enabled.
Journey: Installer captures representative fence approaches, crossings and ordinary nearby movement. > Reviewer labels these clips and approves a threshold for the site. > AiWAS detects a candidate climb sequence and saves the complete approach and landing interval where visible. > Operator checks whether a climb occurred and whether maintenance explains it. > Confirmed entry follows the intrusion procedure; unclear clips remain inconclusive.
Rules: Base the candidate on a motion sequence, not one raised arm. Record the model version and visible evidence. Where the landing is unseen, label the event possible climbing rather than completed crossing.
Exceptions: Ladders, authorised repairs, vegetation and children playing can resemble climbing. Partial bodies or poor night imagery may make the camera unsuitable. Unsupported scenes remain disabled.
Acceptance: Validated test climbs create review alerts. Nearby walking and leaning remain below the agreed false-alert limit. An obscured landing is never reported as a confirmed crossing. Model changes require regression testing.
Scope: Includes visible climbing candidates. Excludes detecting cuts in hidden fences or guaranteeing prevention.
Dependencies: P07 model validation; F002 crossing; F001 response workflow.
Outputs: Sequence clip, fence location, candidate action, model version and human verdict.

title: Crawling or low profile intrusion
Outcome: Detect low-posture human movement in protected areas that an upright-person model may miss.
Inputs: Video, low-posture detector or pose sequence model, protected zones and suitability assessment.
Configure: Select supported postures, minimum visible duration, zone and schedule. Validate object size and night visibility using crawling, crouching, animals and maintenance examples.
Journey: Installer submits representative low-posture clips for validation. > Administrator activates the specialist rule only on approved cameras. > AiWAS identifies a candidate low-profile person in an armed area and opens a review event. > Operator examines the full sequence and distinguishes intrusion, work, injury or an animal. > Operator selects the appropriate security or welfare response and records the outcome.
Rules: Keep posture classification separate from intent. Do not require an upright-person detection as a prerequisite for this specialist detector. Group overlapping upright and low-posture alerts for the same episode.
Exceptions: Workers under equipment, wheelchairs, prams and animals require representative negative tests. Severe occlusion produces uncertainty. A crawling event can need assistance rather than deterrence.
Acceptance: Approved crawling clips are detected without an upright detection. A transition from standing to crawling produces one linked incident. Negative examples meet the documented pilot threshold. Unusable imagery exposes degraded coverage.
Scope: Includes low-posture candidates. Excludes inferring disability, health diagnosis or deliberate evasion.
Dependencies: P07 model validation; P04 grouping; F042 welfare review optional.
Outputs: Posture candidate, visible interval, region, model evidence and response classification.

title: Unauthorised vehicle area entry
Outcome: Detect vehicles entering an area where the configured site policy prohibits that vehicle class.
Inputs: Vehicle tracks, zone geometry, class policy, operating calendar and optional permits.
Configure: Draw pedestrian-only or closed-compound zones; select prohibited classes; add approved delivery windows and expiry-bound exceptions.
Journey: Site manager defines the vehicle policy and tests the zone. > AiWAS detects a vehicle entering during a prohibited period. > Operator sees the vehicle crop, route, policy and any matching permit. > Operator verifies the exception and contacts the gate team or assigned guard. > The incident closes with exit time or the approved exception reference.
Rules: The prohibition comes from the configured area policy. A class uncertainty must remain visible. Emergency or permitted access may be documented by an operator but cannot silently change the permanent rule.
Exceptions: Forklifts, bicycles and mobility devices require explicit classification policies. A vehicle on an adjacent road must not trigger due to a poorly drawn zone. Permit-feed failure shows unknown.
Acceptance: A prohibited vehicle inside the zone creates an event. An allowed class does not. A temporary permit only applies within its effective period. Adjacent-road test traffic is excluded.
Scope: Includes area and class policy enforcement support. Excludes public-road legal enforcement or automatic vehicle immobilisation.
Dependencies: P03 rules; P06 permits optional; F019 dispatch.
Outputs: Vehicle class, prohibited-zone policy, permit context and verification result.

title: Wrong direction movement
Outcome: Detect people or vehicles travelling against a configured one-way route.
Inputs: Object trajectories, lane or corridor region and expected direction vector.
Configure: Draw the route and direction arrow; choose classes, minimum travel distance, persistence and permitted reverse manoeuvre zones.
Journey: Installer confirms the direction arrow with the site manager. > AiWAS follows a qualifying trajectory through the route. > Sustained movement against the arrow produces an event with path and direction. > Operator distinguishes a genuine wrong-way movement from parking or work activity. > Operator contacts the relevant staff and closes after the movement is resolved.
Rules: Require movement over a calibrated distance or validated image displacement; do not flag a single noisy position. Apply turning-zone exclusions. Keep direction confidence separate from class confidence.
Exceptions: Reversing into a bay, turnaround areas and temporary traffic plans need overrides. Camera movement invalidates calibration. Stationary people and vehicles are not wrong-way movement.
Acceptance: A complete counter-direction passage triggers. A stationary object does not. A brief manoeuvre inside an exclusion does not trigger. A temporary direction change applies only to its published schedule.
Scope: Includes configured route deviations. Excludes inferring intent or measuring enforceable traffic offences.
Dependencies: P03 rules; P02 tracking; F078 calibration optional.
Outputs: Expected and observed direction, trajectory, route version and response note.

title: Critical asset approach
Outcome: Give early awareness when a person or vehicle enters a protective area around a critical asset.
Inputs: Asset register, camera zones, object tracks and optional maintenance authorisations.
Configure: Link each asset to warning and restricted zones; define dwell, schedule and distinct severity for each zone. Attach asset-specific instructions and emergency contacts.
Journey: Site manager registers the asset and draws its protective zones. > Installer verifies visible coverage and tests approaches from accessible sides. > AiWAS detects a qualifying approach and shows the asset name and zone severity. > Operator checks maintenance context and reviews the nearby cameras. > Operator follows the asset procedure and documents clearance or intervention.
Rules: Escalate an existing warning episode if it becomes a restricted-zone entry. Do not create multiple unrelated incidents for the same approach. Asset maintenance windows must expire automatically.
Exceptions: Routine workers or service vehicles may be authorised. Cameras cannot establish tampering with hidden components. Assets moved within the scene require zone review.
Acceptance: Warning-zone entry produces the configured lower severity. Restricted-zone progression escalates the same episode. An expired maintenance window no longer suppresses alerts. Missing asset instructions block production activation.
Scope: Includes proximity and zone escalation. Excludes diagnosing asset faults or damage from proximity alone.
Dependencies: P03 asset rules; P04 escalation; F026 work orders optional.
Outputs: Asset ID, approach path, highest reached zone, maintenance context and outcome.

title: Night time and large area protection
Outcome: Combine suitable visual, thermal or radar observations into a reviewable perimeter incident.
Inputs: Supported sensor streams or events, sensor locations, calibration, timestamps and linked verification cameras.
Configure: Register each sensor's coverage and coordinate mapping; choose corroboration windows, source priorities and single-sensor fallback policy. Document tested weather and distance limits.
Journey: Installer commissions each sensor independently and tests shared coverage. > Administrator publishes the correlation and fallback policy. > A sensor detects an object; AiWAS opens the relevant camera and seeks corroborating observations. > Operator sees which sensors support the event and which are unavailable. > Operator verifies and responds; unresolved sensor health issues create maintenance tasks.
Rules: Preserve source events and their uncertainty. Correlation requires compatible time and location. A non-detection by a sensor with poor coverage does not cancel another source's alert. PTZ movement must not remove all fixed coverage.
Exceptions: Fog, thermal crossover, radar multipath and network delay may reduce reliability. Missing calibration disables fused position claims. Unsynchronised clocks mark correlation uncertain.
Acceptance: A staged multi-sensor crossing yields one linked incident. Sensor failure follows the configured fallback and exposes degradation. Events at different locations are not merged merely because their timestamps match.
Scope: Includes sensor orchestration and verification. Excludes a blanket all-weather guarantee or autonomous pursuit outside the site.
Dependencies: P06 sensor connectors; P02 video; P07 commissioning; F081 health.
Outputs: Source event IDs, correlation rationale, confidence by source, verification camera and incident outcome.

title: AI assisted virtual patrols
Outcome: Complete scheduled camera patrols and record evidence-backed findings for every required checkpoint.
Inputs: Patrol template, ordered cameras, expected conditions, schedule, operator assignment and supported visual checks.
Configure: Define checkpoints such as gate closed or yard clear, observation duration, due window, retry policy and escalation. Separate AI-checkable conditions from mandatory human checks.
Journey: Supervisor creates and previews a patrol route. > At the scheduled time AiWAS creates a patrol run and captures the required views. > AI proposes checkpoint findings with evidence; operator reviews exceptions and mandatory checks. > Operator marks each checkpoint passed, issue found or unable to inspect and creates incidents for issues. > Supervisor receives a completion record with missed checkpoints and follow-up tasks.
Rules: A patrol completes only when every checkpoint has a terminal status. Unable to inspect is not passed. Late completion retains the original due time. Reopening creates a new revision without replacing the first result.
Exceptions: Offline cameras cause incomplete coverage and escalation. Overlapping patrols must not share evidence outside their allowed time window. Operator absence triggers reassignment.
Acceptance: A five-checkpoint run retains five individual results. One unavailable camera prevents an all-passed result. A late run is labelled late. A detected issue links to an incident with its original clip.
Scope: Includes scheduled inspections and human confirmation. Excludes replacing physical inspections of invisible conditions.
Dependencies: P02 video; P05 jobs; P04 incidents; F081 health.
Outputs: Patrol run, checkpoint evidence, reviewer, completion status, exceptions and linked incidents.

title: Alarm video verification
Outcome: Bring the correct video and site procedure to an operator when an external alarm arrives.
Inputs: Alarm provider events, device-to-camera mapping, capture times, alarm type and site response instructions.
Configure: Map each alarm device to primary and secondary cameras; set pre-event and post-event clip windows, urgency and escalation. Test sample signals before enabling live routing.
Journey: Integration administrator connects and tests the alarm feed. > An alarm arrives; AiWAS deduplicates the source event and requests mapped video. > Operator opens the incident containing the source signal, live views and recorded evidence. > Operator marks verified threat, explained activity, false alarm or unverifiable and adds a reason. > Any required dispatch follows the approved procedure; closure includes both the signal and verification outcome.
Rules: Never drop the original alarm because video is unavailable. Keep source alarm state independent of AiWAS incident state. Source retries must not duplicate incidents. Alarm cancellation does not erase earlier evidence.
Exceptions: Missing camera mapping shows an actionable configuration error. Clock differences widen retrieval or label timing uncertainty. Delayed clips appear as pending rather than blank evidence.
Acceptance: Duplicate delivery produces one incident. A mapped test signal retrieves the correct camera interval. Offline video produces unverifiable with escalation. Source reset does not close an incident requiring review.
Scope: Includes verification assistance. Excludes assuming authority to reset alarms or contact emergency services automatically.
Dependencies: P06 connectors; P02 clips; P04 incident lifecycle.
Outputs: Original alarm, retrieval status, operator verdict, dispatch reference and audit history.

title: Nuisance alarm filtering
Outcome: Reduce irrelevant video alerts while preserving visibility of filtered decisions and missed-event risk.
Inputs: Candidate motion events, associated video, supported class detector and validated per-camera thresholds.
Configure: Select eligible low-risk event types, target classes and uncertainty handling. Start in shadow mode, displaying what would be filtered without suppressing delivery.
Journey: Supervisor enables shadow evaluation on representative cameras. > AiWAS labels candidate events and records proposed pass or filter decisions. > Reviewer samples both groups and checks missed relevant activity. > Supervisor approves a versioned policy; qualifying events enter the operator queue while filtered events remain auditable. > Drift or poor performance triggers threshold review or rollback.
Rules: Filter only approved event classes. Duress, fire-system and other designated critical source alarms bypass this filter. Uncertain analysis passes to review. Retain decision metadata for the approved audit period.
Exceptions: No clip, model timeout or poor image quality must use fail-open routing for eligible security alerts. Animals resembling people and headlights in rain belong in validation data.
Acceptance: A missing model response still delivers the event. A critical alarm bypasses filtering. Shadow mode suppresses nothing. Reviewers can retrieve sampled filtered decisions and the exact model version.
Scope: Includes relevance filtering. Excludes claiming zero false alarms or deleting source events.
Dependencies: P07 evaluation; P03 rules; P04 routing; F081 health.
Outputs: Filter decision, reason, confidence, policy version and sampled-review outcome.

title: Incident grouping
Outcome: Present related detections as one operational incident while retaining each original event.
Inputs: Event IDs, site, times, zones, camera adjacency, track associations and open incidents.
Configure: Choose grouping windows, compatible event types, adjacent zones and maximum incident duration. Allow strict separation for critical sources.
Journey: Administrator previews grouping on historical events. > AiWAS receives an event and checks eligible open incidents in the same customer and site. > A related event is attached with a reason; otherwise a new incident opens. > Operator reviews the combined timeline and can split or merge incidents with justification. > Closure preserves all event links and the grouping history.
Rules: Never group across customers. Time proximity alone is insufficient where locations differ. New critical evidence raises severity without silently lowering it later. Human splits override automatic regrouping for the same events.
Exceptions: Late events attach with capture and arrival times. Camera clock uncertainty may prevent association. Separate simultaneous incidents must remain independently assignable.
Acceptance: Two adjacent-camera observations of one staged episode group. Simultaneous unrelated zones remain separate under the configured policy. A manual split persists. No event is lost after merge and unmerge operations.
Scope: Includes event association and reversible operator correction. Excludes asserting identity solely from similar appearance.
Dependencies: P04 incidents; P02 timestamps; F034 associations optional.
Outputs: Incident membership, grouping rationale, severity changes and correction audit trail.

title: Alarm prioritisation
Outcome: Order the incident queue according to explicit urgency rules and response obligations.
Inputs: Event type, asset criticality, site policy, corroboration, incident age and response deadlines.
Configure: Define severity levels, rule precedence, response targets and supervisor override permissions. Show example events at each level before publication.
Journey: Supervisor assigns policies to sites. > An incident receives a priority and a human-readable explanation. > Operator sees the highest-priority work with age and deadline indicators. > New corroboration or elapsed time can escalate the incident and notify a supervisor. > Operator or supervisor records justified overrides; reports compare response performance by severity.
Rules: Critical source alarms must not be demoted by low AI confidence. Ageing prevents low-priority work from disappearing indefinitely. A priority change is versioned and cannot erase a missed deadline.
Exceptions: Missing site policy uses an explicit fallback and configuration warning. Notification failure triggers another configured channel. Bulk changes require preview because they affect live queues.
Acceptance: A critical alarm appears above routine events. An aged event escalates at the configured boundary. Manual override records actor and reason. Missing policy never leaves an incident unrouted.
Scope: Includes operational queue ranking. Excludes personal risk scores or prediction of criminality.
Dependencies: P04 incidents; P03 policies; P05 notifications; F085 metrics.
Outputs: Priority, contributing rules, response deadlines, escalations and override history.

title: Remote voice intervention
Outcome: Let an authorised operator address people through a mapped site speaker during a verified incident.
Inputs: Live camera, speaker or intercom endpoint, incident, site script and device permissions.
Configure: Map speakers to visible areas; define approved messages, live-talk permissions and permitted hours. Test volume and location without a live security event.
Journey: Operator verifies the scene and selects the mapped speaker. > AiWAS shows the speaker location, audience area and connection state. > Operator chooses an approved message or starts permitted live speech. > The system sends a bounded command and displays acknowledgement or failure. > Operator watches the response, repeats only if appropriate, and records the result in the incident.
Rules: Require explicit operator action for live intervention. One active speaking session per endpoint avoids conflicting instructions. Command expiry prevents delayed playback. Delivery acknowledgement does not prove the person heard the message.
Exceptions: Offline speaker offers another response path. Incorrect mapping requires suspension. Audio recording is off unless a configured lawful policy permits it; log command metadata regardless.
Acceptance: An unauthorised user cannot speak. An expired queued command never plays. A failed endpoint does not display delivered. Concurrent talk attempts show the current session owner.
Scope: Includes approved verbal intervention. Excludes threatening generated speech, autonomous confrontation or emergency broadcast certification.
Dependencies: P06 device commands; P04 incidents; P01 permissions.
Outputs: Message or session reference, initiator, device acknowledgement, time and observed outcome.

title: Remote employee escort
Outcome: Support an employee-requested video escort along an agreed site route.
Inputs: Authenticated request, agreed route, available cameras, communication channel and escort operator.
Configure: Publish supported routes, service hours, maximum duration, handover points and assistance escalation. Show known blind spots to the requester.
Journey: Employee requests an escort and chooses a supported destination. > Operator accepts, confirms the starting point through the approved channel and checks camera availability. > AiWAS opens route cameras; operator follows the agreed journey with the employee's awareness. > Loss of contact or an incident triggers the escort procedure and, if needed, guard dispatch. > Employee or operator confirms arrival; the session closes and temporary tracking context expires.
Rules: Escort is bounded to the requested route and session. A camera handover suggestion is not proof of identity. Require explicit arrival confirmation rather than assuming success when the person disappears.
Exceptions: Uncovered route offers physical escort or another agreed service. Connection loss remains an unresolved session. Cancellation records who cancelled and whether a welfare check is needed.
Acceptance: A request outside service hours shows an alternative. Arrival confirmation closes the session. Camera loss raises a visible interruption. Closed sessions cannot continue live person-following without a new request.
Scope: Includes requested on-site escorts. Excludes continuous off-site tracking.
Dependencies: P04 session workflow; P02 cameras; F019 dispatch optional.
Outputs: Escort request, route, operator, interruptions, arrival or cancellation outcome.

title: Opening and closing checks
Outcome: Verify a site's configured opening or closing checklist using visible evidence and connected device status.
Inputs: Site checklist, cameras, optional door contacts, opening calendar and responsible staff.
Configure: Define each required condition, its evidence source, due time and escalation. Mark checks requiring human confirmation; distinguish visible closed from electronically secured.
Journey: Supervisor builds the site checklist and tests evidence sources. > AiWAS starts the scheduled run and proposes observable results. > Operator reviews gates, doors, occupied areas and required manual checks. > Failed or unknown conditions become tasks assigned to the site contact. > Operator completes the run only after each condition has a documented outcome; unresolved exceptions remain visible.
Rules: Camera appearance cannot prove a lock is engaged. A locked claim requires a trusted lock-status source. An empty visible area is not proof that the entire building is empty. Overrides require named responsibility.
Exceptions: Cleaning or late work requires an expiring exception. Device disagreement is flagged. Offline views produce unknown checks and a follow-up task.
Acceptance: An apparently closed door with an unlocked sensor fails a secure-door check. One unknown item prevents an all-clear. A late-worker exception expires at its configured time.
Scope: Includes checklist orchestration. Excludes automatic security certification or autonomous arming without an authorised integration policy.
Dependencies: F011 patrol runs; P06 door status; P04 tasks.
Outputs: Checklist results, evidence, overrides, unresolved tasks and completion sign-off.

title: Guard dispatch assistance
Outcome: Assign a verified incident to a guard and maintain a clear response status through completion.
Inputs: Incident location, response procedure, available guard roster, contact channel and optional on-duty location.
Configure: Set eligible teams, coverage areas, acknowledgement deadline, reassignment rules and required completion fields. Limit location collection to approved on-duty use.
Journey: Dispatcher reviews the incident and selects an eligible guard or team. > Guard receives the location, safe access instructions, clip and task priority. > Guard accepts or declines with a reason; unacknowledged tasks escalate. > Guard records en route, arrived and action taken, attaching evidence where authorised. > Dispatcher reviews the result, resolves outstanding work and closes the task and incident separately.
Rules: Assignment is not acceptance. Arrival needs an explicit event or approved verified integration. Reassignment revokes the previous active assignment while retaining history. Guard safety instructions must remain available when video cannot load.
Exceptions: Offline mobile clients queue safe updates with device and receipt times. A declined assignment returns to dispatch. Concurrent assignment changes use version checks to avoid conflicting owners.
Acceptance: A missed acknowledgement escalates once per policy step. Reassignment updates both users. Offline status sync preserves order and timestamps. Closing a task does not erase an unresolved incident.
Scope: Includes dispatch coordination. Excludes autonomous emergency-service dispatch and guarantees about guard response.
Dependencies: P04 tasks; P05 delivery; P01 guard roles; F085 timings.
Outputs: Assignment history, response statuses, timestamps, guard notes and completion evidence.

title: Incident and shift reports
Outcome: Produce editable reports grounded in verified incidents, actions and linked evidence.
Inputs: Incident records, operator notes, dispatch events, shift boundaries and reporting template.
Configure: Choose required sections, customer visibility, review owner, timezone and approved vocabulary. Select whether reports include unresolved and dismissed events.
Journey: Supervisor selects a shift or incident and generates a draft. > AiWAS assembles facts and links each material statement to its record or clip. > Reviewer checks the draft, edits language and resolves unsupported statements. > Reviewer approves a version and exports or publishes it to authorised recipients. > Corrections create a new version with change history and, where necessary, recipient notification.
Rules: Generated text cannot change incident verdicts. Separate observations, operator decisions and unresolved questions. Missing evidence must be stated rather than filled in. Publication requires human approval in the initial release.
Exceptions: Incomplete incidents appear as open. Redacted users or footage must remain redacted in narrative and attachments. Generation failure preserves source data and allows manual reporting.
Acceptance: Every factual event claim has a source reference. A report with unresolved placeholders cannot publish. Cross-customer records are excluded. A corrected version preserves the original approved version.
Scope: Includes draft generation, review and export. Excludes legal conclusions, invented identities and automatic external distribution.
Dependencies: P08 evidence; P04 incidents; P09 reporting; F039 export.
Outputs: Draft, approved report version, source links, reviewer and publication audit.

title: Door tailgating
Outcome: Identify possible extra entries associated with a single access grant.
Inputs: Door access grants, door state, directional person counts and aligned camera timestamps.
Configure: Map door and camera; set grant matching window, allowed persons per grant and special group-entry policy. Commission counts for the doorway.
Journey: Administrator tests single-person and group entries. > A credential grant opens a correlation window. > AiWAS counts inward crossings and flags excess entries with the associated grant. > Operator reviews the sequence and checks group permissions or accessibility assistance. > Confirmed exceptions go to the site team; the verdict is retained for tuning.
Rules: Count entries rather than nearby people. Multiple grants can cover multiple people within the matching policy. A candidate does not identify which person lacked authorisation. Public operating hours can use a separate policy.
Exceptions: Occlusion or access-feed loss produces indeterminate correlation. Children, carers and escorted groups require explicit rules. A held-open door can create a separate F023 event.
Acceptance: Two inward crossings on a one-person grant create a candidate. Two matching grants cover two entries. Outward movement is excluded. A missing access feed cannot label a person unauthorised.
Scope: Includes count-to-grant comparison. Excludes automatic accusation or door closure on a person.
Dependencies: P06 access connector; F002 crossings; F023 door context.
Outputs: Grant IDs, directional counts, mismatch interval, video and operator verdict.

title: Vehicle gate tailgating
Outcome: Flag multiple vehicles passing a controlled gate on one approved opening cycle.
Inputs: Gate cycle events, vehicle trajectories, lane geometry and authorisation records.
Configure: Map each lane and gate; define allowed vehicles per cycle, articulated-vehicle treatment and closing-window logic.
Journey: Installer validates cars, trailers and motorcycles through the lane. > AiWAS opens a cycle when the gate grants entry. > Vehicle crossings are associated with that cycle and compared with allowed passage. > Operator reviews excess passages and available plate records. > Gate staff receive a follow-up task and the event closes with the actual disposition.
Rules: A tractor and attached trailer must not automatically count as two independent vehicles. Reopening and held-open cycles must remain distinguishable. Never close a barrier merely to stop a suspected second vehicle.
Exceptions: Congested lanes and partial views can make counts uncertain. Lost gate state prevents definitive grant comparison. Emergency open mode is explicitly recorded.
Acceptance: Two separate cars on one grant create a candidate. A validated articulated truck is one passage. Emergency open mode follows its configured policy. Offline gate state shows unknown correlation.
Scope: Includes lane passage exceptions. Excludes collision-prone automated barrier intervention.
Dependencies: P06 gate connector; F071 plate logs optional; F002 crossings.
Outputs: Cycle ID, passage count, vehicle clips, authorisations and review outcome.

title: Door held open verification
Outcome: Explain and resolve a door-held-open alarm using video and door state.
Inputs: Door-contact events, open-duration threshold, mapped cameras and delivery or maintenance windows.
Configure: Set door-specific thresholds and urgency; link the nearest verification views and responsible site contact.
Journey: Door remains open beyond its permitted interval. > AiWAS opens an incident with elapsed time and nearby video. > Operator checks whether a person, delivery or object explains the open door. > Operator contacts the responsible staff and observes the response. > Door-closed evidence resolves the condition; operator closes the incident after documenting exceptions.
Rules: A contact supplies physical open state; video adds context. An alarm ending is different from operator closure. Continue displaying elapsed duration while open. Approved exceptions have expiry and owner.
Exceptions: Faulty contacts can disagree with video and require maintenance. Repeated open-close oscillation needs debouncing. Lost status must not be interpreted as closed.
Acceptance: Threshold crossing opens one episode. A closed contact ends the condition but retains review history. Missing contact updates show stale state. Expired delivery exceptions no longer suppress events.
Scope: Includes verification and follow-up. Excludes remote locking unless separately authorised and integrated.
Dependencies: P06 door connector; P04 incident lifecycle; F018 closing checks.
Outputs: Open interval, contact state, observed explanation, exception and resolution evidence.

title: Forced door incident reconstruction
Outcome: Reconstruct access activity surrounding a forced-door signal without confusing the signal with proof of forced entry.
Inputs: Forced-door event, access grants, lock and contact states, video and device clock offsets.
Configure: Map door sources and cameras; select retrieval windows and evidence retention for this incident type.
Journey: Source system raises a forced-door signal. > AiWAS retrieves pre-event and post-event footage and nearby access events. > Operator verifies the current situation and initiates any required response. > Investigator aligns the timeline, reviews conflicting records and records the supported sequence. > Investigator saves an evidence package and closes or refers the case.
Rules: Preserve the source's wording and raw payload. Display capture time, device time and any correction. Do not rewrite a hardware signal as a confirmed human action. Timeline edits are annotations, not changes to originals.
Exceptions: Misconfigured contacts and clock drift can explain apparent discrepancies. Missing footage remains a visible gap. A delayed source event must not look like a current live breach.
Acceptance: A test signal retrieves the correct interval. Known clock offset is displayed. Missing video appears as a gap. An investigator can export original records alongside annotations.
Scope: Includes reconstruction and response support. Excludes establishing legal culpability.
Dependencies: P06 access; F012 verification; F037 timeline; F039 evidence.
Outputs: Door-event timeline, video references, timing uncertainties and investigator findings.

title: Visitor overstays
Outcome: Identify active visitor records extending beyond their authorised visit window and verify whether the visitor remains on site.
Inputs: Visit authorisation, check-in and checkout records, host, expiry and optional controlled exit observations.
Configure: Set grace period, reminder timing, host escalation and checkout evidence requirements by visitor type.
Journey: Reception creates a visit and its end time. > Visitor checks in and receives the approved access method. > Near expiry, host receives a reminder; after grace, AiWAS opens an overstay task. > Reception or operator contacts the host and checks available records before concluding the visitor remains. > Staff record departure, approve an extension or escalate the unresolved visit.
Rules: An unclosed visit is a record exception, not proof of physical presence. Extensions require an authorised host and effective expiry. Do not silently infer checkout from a lookalike on video.
Exceptions: Forgotten checkout, group visits and emergency evacuation require reconciliation. Host unavailability triggers reception fallback. Feed delays retain both event and receipt times.
Acceptance: An active expired visit creates one task. A verified earlier checkout prevents an overstay. An approved extension changes the deadline with audit. Missing checkout remains unconfirmed presence.
Scope: Includes visit lifecycle and verification. Excludes continuous visitor tracking outside approved areas.
Dependencies: P06 visitor system; P05 reminders; P04 tasks.
Outputs: Visit status, reminder history, extension or departure evidence and unresolved exception.

title: Contractor access exceptions
Outcome: Compare contractor entry with approved work, time and destination restrictions.
Inputs: Work order, contractor authorisation, access events, camera observations and permit validity.
Configure: Map work orders to sites, permitted zones, entry windows and responsible supervisors. Define the policy for an unavailable permit source.
Journey: Site manager approves a work order and access window. > Contractor arrives; AiWAS retrieves the relevant authorisation alongside the entrance view. > An early, late or wrong-zone event creates an exception for review. > Operator contacts the work supervisor and records approval, redirection or refusal under site policy. > Departure and work completion close the access record; temporary permissions expire.
Rules: A visible uniform is not proof of contractor authorisation. Only approved roles can extend access. Revoked permits must take effect according to the connector freshness policy.
Exceptions: Emergency repairs need an audited emergency workflow. Cached permits show their age. A missing work-order match is unknown until reviewed, not proof of wrongdoing.
Acceptance: Valid in-window access matches the permit. Wrong-zone access produces an exception. Revocation invalidates the permit within the contracted sync interval. An emergency override records approver and expiry.
Scope: Includes authorisation comparison. Excludes certifying qualifications or safety compliance from appearance.
Dependencies: P06 work orders and access; F003 zones; P01 permissions.
Outputs: Work-order match, exception type, approval trail and access completion.

title: Visitor escort separation
Outcome: Flag possible separation of an assigned visitor and escort inside specifically monitored controlled areas.
Inputs: Approved visit and escort pairing, camera tracks, permitted route and calibrated separation observations.
Configure: Set monitored zones, visible separation duration, allowed waiting points and track-confidence requirements. Explain monitoring to participants through the site's visit process.
Journey: Reception registers the visitor and escort relationship. > Operator or a controlled entry event establishes the starting pair. > AiWAS monitors supported camera views for sustained separation. > Operator reviews the candidate and checks whether a permitted handover or waiting arrangement explains it. > Staff reunite the pair, update the escort or dismiss the candidate with evidence.
Rules: Uncertain cross-camera identity cannot support a confirmed separation. Temporary occlusion becomes tracking unknown. Pairing expires at visit completion. Distance thresholds require calibrated geometry.
Exceptions: Lifts, toilets and blind corridors interrupt observation; they are not automatic breaches. Group escorts require explicit allowed group size and pairing logic.
Acceptance: A staged visible separation beyond the limit creates a candidate. A permitted waiting point does not. Losing sight of one person shows unknown. Visit completion removes the active pairing.
Scope: Includes bounded visit supervision. Excludes tracking visitors across unrelated sites or private areas.
Dependencies: F025 visits; F034 optional associations; P07 validation.
Outputs: Pair reference, observed separation interval, coverage gaps and operator decision.

title: Credential and entry mismatch
Outcome: Reconcile access grants and observed doorway passages to find operational discrepancies.
Inputs: Access-grant and denial events, directional counts, door cycles and time alignment.
Configure: Define mismatch types: grant without passage, passage without grant and count imbalance. Set matching windows and allowed group policies.
Journey: Administrator tests synchronisation and doorway counting. > AiWAS associates grants and passages during each window. > A mismatch creates a review task with both records and the relevant clip. > Operator checks whether the cause is unused access, a system fault, group entry or a security exception. > Confirmed causes route to maintenance or security and update the reconciliation record.
Rules: Keep this reconciler distinct from F021's live excess-entry alarm. Each grant and passage has explicit matching status. Do not reuse a grant across independent episodes unless policy permits it.
Exceptions: A person opening a door without entering is often legitimate. Denied credentials and authorised manual openings require separate event types. Delayed feeds can change provisional mismatches.
Acceptance: A grant without passage becomes a discrepancy after the window closes. A late matching event resolves a provisional mismatch with history. One grant cannot silently cover two unrelated episodes.
Scope: Includes reconciliation. Excludes identifying a credential borrower from video alone.
Dependencies: P06 access; F021 counts; P04 tasks.
Outputs: Matched and unmatched event pairs, provisional or final status and resolution reason.

title: Remote reception and entry approval
Outcome: Let authorised remote staff handle an entrance request using live video, intercom and current visit authorisation.
Inputs: Intercom request, entrance camera, visitor record, host confirmation and access-controller command interface.
Configure: Map entrance devices; set service hours, approval roles, command timeout and local fallback. Keep emergency egress independent.
Journey: Visitor calls at the entrance. > Receptionist accepts and sees live video and the matching visit record. > Receptionist checks identity through the approved process and obtains any required host approval. > Receptionist explicitly selects admit; AiWAS sends an expiring command and shows controller acknowledgement. > Entry is logged and the session closes; failed admission is escalated to local staff.
Rules: Do not treat a video match as authorisation. The access controller retains physical safety interlocks. Prevent duplicate release commands from double-clicks or retries. Record approval before command issue.
Exceptions: Stale video, missing visit or lost intercom requires manual fallback. A command timeout is unknown outcome until controller status is checked. Do not blindly resend uncertain commands.
Acceptance: An unprivileged user cannot admit. Duplicate clicks produce one command. Timeout shows uncertain outcome. Host refusal prevents admission through this workflow.
Scope: Includes remote reception. Excludes bypassing access-controller safety or emergency-egress requirements.
Dependencies: P06 intercom and access; P01 command permissions; F025 visits.
Outputs: Call record, verification result, approver, release-command status and entry event.

title: Optional biometric verification
Outcome: Verify a person's claimed enrolled identity at a controlled access point where the deployment has an approved lawful basis.
Inputs: Claimed identity or credential, authorised enrolment template, suitable camera and validated presentation-attack checks.
Configure: Enable only for approved sites; set matching threshold, retry limit, retention, enrolment authority and an equivalent non-biometric alternative.
Journey: Administrator approves the deployment and enrolment procedure. > User enrols through the approved process and receives information on use and deletion. > At entry the user claims an identity; the system captures a suitable sample and performs one-to-one verification. > Success supplies a verification result to the access policy; failure offers retry or an alternative. > User departure from the programme triggers revocation and scheduled template deletion.
Rules: Verification does not itself grant access. No one-to-many watchlist search is included. Encrypt templates separately, restrict export and audit access. Test relevant image conditions and demographic performance before release.
Exceptions: Poor image, presentation attack or unavailable service cannot auto-approve. Withdrawal or expiry removes eligibility under the approved policy. Accessibility requires a usable alternative.
Acceptance: A verified claim still fails entry if its access permission is revoked. Deleted enrolments cannot match. Replay attempts follow the validated attack-test policy. Alternative access remains available.
Scope: Includes controlled one-to-one verification only. Excludes public face scanning, sensitive-attribute inference and cross-client identity databases.
Dependencies: P01 special permissions; P07 biometric validation; P08 retention; P06 access.
Outputs: Verification result, reason category and audit reference; raw samples retained only under the approved policy.

title: Search footage using plain language
Outcome: Retrieve candidate footage from a bounded authorised search expressed in ordinary language.
Inputs: Indexed video metadata or embeddings, user query, permitted cameras, time range and optional case reference.
Configure: Choose supported query concepts, indexed retention window, query limits and result ranking. Keep unsupported attributes visibly unsupported.
Journey: Investigator opens Search, selects a case, cameras and period, then enters a query. > AiWAS displays its interpretation as editable filters before execution. > Search runs asynchronously and returns ranked clips with timestamps and coverage status. > Investigator watches candidates, marks relevant results and refines the query. > Selected original clips attach to the case with query and retrieval history.
Rules: Results are candidates, not factual answers. An empty result means nothing matched in indexed coverage, not that the event never happened. Enforce permissions during retrieval and clip playback. Never execute instructions found inside footage or metadata.
Exceptions: Unindexed periods, unavailable cameras and unsupported queries appear explicitly. Large searches can be cancelled. Index deletion must propagate to search results.
Acceptance: A query containing a known staged event retrieves it within the agreed top-K benchmark. Excluded cameras never appear. Partial indexing is labelled. A result links to the exact original interval.
Scope: Includes retrieval and refinement. Excludes identifying people from sensitive traits or generating missing footage.
Dependencies: P02 indexing; P01 access; P05 search jobs; P07 retrieval evaluation.
Outputs: Query interpretation, result set, ranking version, coverage and saved evidence selections.

title: Person appearance search
Outcome: Find candidate sightings using visible clothing and carried-object attributes within an authorised investigation.
Inputs: Person detections, supported appearance attributes, optional reference crop, camera and time filters.
Configure: Enable validated attributes such as upper clothing colour, lower clothing colour and bag presence; define minimum image quality and search retention.
Journey: Investigator selects the case and search area. > Investigator chooses visible attributes or an authorised reference crop. > AiWAS returns matching candidates with confidence and original timestamps. > Investigator inspects clips and rejects lookalikes before saving relevant sightings. > Saved results remain evidence candidates until the investigator records their conclusion.
Rules: Clothing similarity does not establish identity. Do not infer sensitive attributes. Night infrared imagery may not support true colour and must be labelled accordingly. Keep the reference's provenance.
Exceptions: Occluded clothing, uniforms and lighting changes reduce discrimination. Different outfits can cause missed sightings. A deleted or inaccessible source crop cannot remain available through search cache.
Acceptance: Supported colour filters apply to eligible imagery. Infrared results do not claim reliable visible colour. A saved candidate retains its source and timestamp. Permissions apply to reference uploads and results.
Scope: Includes observable appearance filtering. Excludes identity proof and unrestricted person monitoring.
Dependencies: P02 metadata; P07 attribute evaluation; P08 case evidence.
Outputs: Search filters, candidate crops, clips, uncertainty and investigator selections.

title: Vehicle appearance search
Outcome: Find vehicles in recorded footage by supported visible characteristics.
Inputs: Vehicle detections, class and colour attributes, optional reference image and bounded search scope.
Configure: Publish supported vehicle classes and any validated make/model capabilities. Keep plate search separate from appearance similarity.
Journey: Investigator selects site, cameras and dates. > Investigator enters known class, colour or a reference image. > AiWAS returns candidates with attribute confidence and image-quality notes. > Investigator reviews full clips and optionally cross-checks plate records. > Relevant candidates attach to the case with original provenance.
Rules: A class or colour match is not a unique vehicle match. Do not fabricate make/model when unsupported. Preserve different hypotheses where the image cannot distinguish classes.
Exceptions: Night lighting, covered vehicles, trailers and partial views may produce unknown attributes. Multiple similar fleet vehicles require corroboration. Missing index ranges are displayed.
Acceptance: Class filtering retrieves the labelled test set at the approved benchmark. Unsupported make/model filters cannot be enabled. Similar vehicles remain separate candidates. A selected result opens the original clip.
Scope: Includes appearance retrieval. Excludes ownership lookup or unique identification without corroboration.
Dependencies: P02 index; F071 plate records optional; P08 cases.
Outputs: Vehicle candidates, attribute scores, source clips and selected case links.

title: Incident scoped cross camera tracing
Outcome: Help reconstruct a candidate route across authorised site cameras for one defined investigation.
Inputs: Selected sighting, camera adjacency map, time windows, appearance associations and case purpose.
Configure: Define permitted sites, plausible travel times, association thresholds and case expiry. Default to same-site use with explicit scope selection.
Journey: Investigator selects a verified starting clip within a case. > AiWAS suggests next and previous candidate sightings with alternative paths. > Investigator watches each clip and accepts or rejects each link. > The route view distinguishes accepted links, AI suggestions and unseen gaps. > Investigator saves the reviewed route and closes the tracing session.
Rules: Never present a suggested link as confirmed identity. Enforce physically plausible travel times without inventing movement through blind spots. Preserve rejected links and reviewer actions. Reopening requires a still-authorised case.
Exceptions: Uniforms, crowds and lookalikes can create ambiguity. Clock errors weaken sequence claims. A path can stop when confidence is inadequate rather than forcing a complete route.
Acceptance: Impossible travel-time links are excluded or flagged. Rejected links do not silently reappear as accepted. Every route segment opens original footage. Out-of-scope cameras remain unavailable.
Scope: Includes bounded investigative association. Excludes persistent cross-client tracking and public movement profiling.
Dependencies: F032 or F033; P07 association validation; P08 case permissions.
Outputs: Candidate route graph, accepted and rejected links, gaps, provenance and reviewer history.

title: Missing person search assistance
Outcome: Help an authorised facility team locate candidate sightings in response to a reported missing person.
Inputs: Incident report, authorised reference description or image, last confirmed sighting and facility cameras.
Configure: Set emergency search roles, geographic limits, expiry, contact procedure and handling of sensitive reference information.
Journey: Operator records the report and confirms the reporter through the facility procedure. > Operator starts a time-bounded search from the last confirmed location. > AiWAS returns candidates and visible route suggestions, with uncertainties. > Operator verifies sightings and dispatches staff to check locations without exposing unnecessary personal data. > A responsible human confirms the person is found; search alerts stop and references follow retention policy.
Rules: Finding requires human confirmation. Do not infer vulnerability or age from appearance. Keep live search restricted to the active incident. Do not provide location access to an unverified requester.
Exceptions: No matches or blind spots require wider manual search, not reassurance. Multiple similar people remain distinct. False or disputed reports require supervisor review.
Acceptance: Closing the incident stops live candidate notifications. An unverified requester cannot receive location results. No-result output displays camera coverage gaps. Dispatch references the verified candidate location and time.
Scope: Includes facility incident assistance. Excludes unrestricted tracking or identity conclusions from appearance.
Dependencies: F032; F034 optional; F019 dispatch; P08 sensitive evidence.
Outputs: Report, search scope, verified sightings, dispatched checks and confirmed resolution.

title: Object appearance or removal search
Outcome: Find when a visible object first appeared or disappeared from a selected scene region.
Inputs: Recorded video, object reference or region, time range and usable scene baseline.
Configure: Select the object area, persistence threshold and expected scene stability. Choose appearance, removal or both; specify any known object class.
Journey: Investigator opens the relevant camera and marks the object or location. > AiWAS scans the selected interval for sustained scene changes. > Candidate transitions appear with before-and-after frames and surrounding clips. > Investigator checks occlusion, cleaning or legitimate movement and selects the supported transition. > The selected interval and uncertainty attach to the case.
Rules: A hidden object is not necessarily removed. Require persistent absence after visibility returns. Keep first-visible and actual-placement time distinct when the start is outside available footage.
Exceptions: Lighting changes, moved furniture and camera repositioning can invalidate the baseline. Crowded scenes may not support a precise transition. Missing footage yields a time interval rather than an exact claim.
Acceptance: A staged persistent removal returns the transition interval. A person briefly blocking the object does not count as removal. A recording gap is shown in the result. The original before-and-after footage remains accessible.
Scope: Includes visual change search. Excludes inferring ownership, contents or theft.
Dependencies: P02 archive search; P07 scene-change evaluation; P08 cases.
Outputs: Candidate appearance or removal intervals, comparison frames, clips and reviewer selection.

title: Incident timeline assembly
Outcome: Build a chronological view of evidence and actions without changing source timestamps or records.
Inputs: Camera events, clips, access records, guard updates, operator notes and clock-offset metadata.
Configure: Choose case sources, display timezone, timing precision and allowed annotation roles.
Journey: Investigator opens a case and selects relevant records. > AiWAS sorts events by normalised capture time and shows timing uncertainty. > Investigator plays linked clips and adds factual annotations or relationships. > Conflicts, gaps and alternate interpretations remain visible. > Investigator approves a timeline version for reporting or evidence export.
Rules: Store original and normalised times separately. Manual time corrections require reason and remain reversible. Distinguish event time, receipt time and note creation time. Do not reorder sources silently to fit a narrative.
Exceptions: Unknown clock offset displays an uncertainty range. Duplicate evidence can be linked once with multiple references. Late evidence creates a new timeline version.
Acceptance: Events from two timezones align correctly. Correcting an offset retains the original timestamp. Late evidence does not overwrite an approved version. Each timeline item resolves to its underlying record.
Scope: Includes chronology and annotations. Excludes claiming causation from temporal proximity.
Dependencies: P08 evidence; P02 time model; F024 access reconstruction.
Outputs: Versioned timeline, source links, annotations, timing gaps and approval record.

title: Condensed footage review
Outcome: Reduce review time by presenting relevant activity segments while preserving the ability to inspect originals.
Inputs: Recorded video, activity intervals, search filters and authorised time range.
Configure: Select event-only playback, playback speed and contextual padding. Initial scope uses chronological segments rather than synthetic simultaneous overlays.
Journey: Investigator selects footage and filtering criteria. > AiWAS builds a review playlist and reports included versus omitted duration. > Investigator plays segments with visible original timestamps and jump-to-original controls. > Investigator expands surrounding context or saves relevant clips. > Review progress and selected evidence are stored with the case.
Rules: Never alter source recordings. Clearly label condensed playback and skipped intervals. Do not imply that separate moments occurred simultaneously. Filtering must be reproducible from saved parameters.
Exceptions: Activity detector misses remain possible; users can inspect the full source. Recording gaps differ from skipped inactivity. Unsupported codecs create a failed item rather than silently disappearing.
Acceptance: Each segment jumps to the correct original timestamp. The playlist preserves chronological order. Omitted intervals are identifiable. A failed source segment is listed in the coverage summary.
Scope: Includes activity playlists and accelerated review. Excludes synthetic evidence reconstruction or patented synopsis implementation assumptions.
Dependencies: P02 indexing and playback; P05 jobs; P08 cases.
Outputs: Playlist, filters, coverage, review progress and selected original evidence.

title: Evidence package creation
Outcome: Export a reproducible set of original records, derivative copies and a manifest for an authorised case.
Inputs: Selected evidence, source identifiers, hashes, case notes, timeline and export permission.
Configure: Define package formats, maximum size, retention or hold, approval requirements and recipient access rules.
Journey: Investigator selects case evidence and checks completeness. > AiWAS validates permissions, source availability and integrity, then shows a package manifest preview. > Investigator or approver confirms the exact contents. > An asynchronous job builds originals, labelled derivatives and a manifest with hashes and provenance. > Authorised user downloads or shares the completed package; access and any later revocation are logged.
Rules: Preserve originals byte-for-byte where obtainable. Label transcoded copies as derivatives and record parent hashes. Hashes support integrity but do not alone establish legal admissibility. A hold must block scheduled deletion of selected originals.
Exceptions: Unavailable evidence blocks complete status or requires an explicitly labelled partial package. Export failure can retry idempotently. Revocation cannot recall copies already downloaded.
Acceptance: Exported originals match stored hashes. Missing evidence appears in the manifest. An unauthorised item cannot enter the package. A partial failure never reports a complete export.
Scope: Includes provenance and controlled export. Excludes a guarantee of court admissibility.
Dependencies: P08 evidence and holds; P05 export jobs; F037 timeline.
Outputs: Package, manifest, integrity checks, export audit and completeness status.

title: Redaction and controlled sharing
Outcome: Share approved evidence copies while obscuring selected people or regions and restricting recipient access.
Inputs: Original video, redaction policy, reviewer selections, recipient identities and share expiry.
Configure: Choose face, body, plate or manual-region redaction; set audio handling and export review requirements. Define viewer versus downloader permissions.
Journey: Reviewer selects evidence and marks sensitive subjects or areas. > AiWAS proposes tracked masks across frames. > Reviewer inspects the full derivative, fixes missed frames and verifies audio treatment. > Reviewer approves a rendered copy and creates an expiring recipient-specific share. > Recipient access is logged; owner can revoke future access and manage retention.
Rules: Originals stay unchanged and restricted. Approval applies to an exact derivative version. Masks must cover entry, exit and occlusion transitions. Do not promise that browser restrictions prevent all screen capture.
Exceptions: Lost mask tracking requires manual correction. Rendering failure cannot publish a partial file. Expiry during viewing must follow documented session behaviour and block new access.
Acceptance: Approved masks persist through the test subject's full visible interval. Unredacted originals are unavailable to derivative-only recipients. Revocation blocks subsequent requests. Re-editing invalidates prior approval for the new copy.
Scope: Includes redaction and access control. Excludes guaranteed recall of downloaded evidence.
Dependencies: P08 derivatives; P01 recipient permissions; P05 rendering jobs.
Outputs: Approved derivative, redaction decisions, share permissions, expiry and access audit.

title: Fall detection
Outcome: Surface an apparent fall quickly and support an appropriate human welfare response.
Inputs: Suitable video, validated temporal fall model, monitored zone and site welfare procedure.
Configure: Approve camera angle and body visibility; set candidate persistence, alert urgency and escalation contacts. Validate falls and ordinary sitting, kneeling and exercise sequences.
Journey: Site manager approves the monitoring area and response procedure. > AiWAS detects a candidate fall sequence and creates an urgent review alert. > Operator watches the sequence and live view, then contacts the person or nearby staff where appropriate. > Operator requests assistance under the site procedure and records actions. > A responsible person confirms the outcome; evidence is retained according to the approved incident policy.
Rules: Use candidate fall wording until verified. Do not wait for identity recognition. A recovery movement does not automatically cancel an unanswered welfare alert. Retain context before the descent.
Exceptions: Occlusion, wheelchairs, deliberate floor work and camera angle affect results. Lost video during an event requires an unresolved welfare task. This is not a clinical diagnosis.
Acceptance: Labelled fall scenarios meet the pilot recall target. Normal sitting meets the false-alert limit. Unacknowledged alerts escalate. Video loss cannot automatically resolve an active welfare event.
Scope: Includes fall candidates and response support. Excludes medical diagnosis or guaranteed fall prevention.
Dependencies: P07 safety validation; P04 urgent incidents; F019 assistance dispatch.
Outputs: Candidate sequence, verification, assistance actions and confirmed outcome.

title: Person down or prolonged immobility
Outcome: Flag a person remaining on the floor or visibly motionless beyond a configured welfare threshold.
Inputs: Person or pose observations, temporal continuity, floor or monitored region and operating context.
Configure: Define qualifying posture, immobility duration, normal rest exclusions and escalation. Distinguish floor presence from ordinary sitting or sleeping in permitted areas.
Journey: Administrator tests the chosen scene and threshold. > AiWAS observes a qualifying posture and starts a visible timer. > Sustained observation creates a welfare candidate with the full interval. > Operator checks live video and seeks a human welfare confirmation. > Staff provide assistance or document an explained activity; operator closes with the outcome.
Rules: Unknown visibility is not immobility. Do not infer breathing, consciousness or cause from ordinary CCTV. Link a preceding F041 event rather than opening unrelated duplicate incidents.
Exceptions: Maintenance work, prayer, exercise and permitted rest need scene context. Track loss suspends certainty. An unresponsive contact attempt escalates according to the welfare procedure.
Acceptance: A visible floor posture beyond the threshold triggers. An occluded person is labelled unknown rather than motionless. A linked fall produces one coordinated incident. Closure requires an explicit outcome.
Scope: Includes observable posture and motion candidates. Excludes clinical monitoring of vital signs.
Dependencies: P07 pose validation; F041 grouping optional; P04 welfare workflow.
Outputs: Posture, duration, observation gaps, contact attempts and welfare outcome.

title: Possible physical altercation
Outcome: Identify movement sequences that may represent a physical altercation for urgent human review.
Inputs: Multi-person temporal video, validated action model, site zones and emergency procedure.
Configure: Set supported scene types, minimum sequence, sensitivity and explicit exclusions for sports or staged activity. Test crowd and playful-contact negatives.
Journey: Site team validates the model on representative footage. > AiWAS surfaces a candidate with preceding and following context. > Operator checks the action and current situation without assigning blame. > Operator follows the site safety response and coordinates trained staff. > Reviewer records confirmed altercation, non-altercation or inconclusive for audit and evaluation.
Rules: Movement alone cannot establish aggression, intent or who initiated contact. A model score must not trigger disciplinary action automatically. Critical response decisions remain with trained staff.
Exceptions: Dancing, sports, embraces, restraint and crowded queues can resemble altercations. Occlusion may prevent a conclusion. Repeated candidates from one continuous episode should group.
Acceptance: Approved staged examples meet documented validation targets. Sports negatives meet the nuisance limit. The UI never labels an individual aggressor automatically. Duplicate sequence windows produce one incident.
Scope: Includes review candidates. Excludes violence prediction, blame assignment and autonomous enforcement.
Dependencies: P07 action-model validation; P04 incidents; F019 dispatch.
Outputs: Candidate sequence, uncertainty, human classification and response record.

title: Visible weapon alerts
Outcome: Surface a potentially visible, specifically supported weapon class for rapid trained verification.
Inputs: Suitable camera imagery, validated specialist detector, supported-class list and approved emergency plan.
Configure: Approve each camera's distance and visibility envelope; set thresholds, verification roles and escalation deadlines. Test common confusing objects and realistic target sizes.
Journey: Specialist reviewer commissions the deployment. > AiWAS detects a candidate object and opens an urgent incident with crop, full frame and live context. > Trained operator reviews promptly and records confirmed, not confirmed or inconclusive. > Operator activates the approved response when warranted; any unverified escalation must follow an explicit preapproved procedure. > Supervisor reviews the handling and outcome after resolution.
Rules: Preserve the full frame, not just a potentially misleading crop. No automatic accusation or police contact is in initial scope. Do not claim detection of concealed weapons. A disappearing object does not erase the event.
Exceptions: Tools, phones and packaging can cause confusion. Tiny, blurred or occluded objects may be undetectable. Operator unavailability must follow a documented backup route.
Acceptance: Candidate alerts include sufficient surrounding context. Confusing-object tests are part of release acceptance. Unanswered incidents escalate to the designated backup. Unsupported classes are never advertised as covered.
Scope: Includes visible supported-class candidates. Excludes concealed-weapon detection and prevention guarantees.
Dependencies: P07 specialist validation; P04 critical handling; P05 escalation.
Outputs: Candidate object, model version, evidence, verifier decision and response timeline.

title: Panic button visual support
Outcome: Immediately present location-specific video and response instructions when someone activates a panic or duress device.
Inputs: Trusted panic event, device location, primary and backup cameras and emergency contacts.
Configure: Map each device, set critical routing and acknowledgement deadlines, and test signals using a clearly separate test mode.
Journey: Administrator commissions the device and response mapping. > A panic activation creates a critical incident regardless of AI interpretation. > Operator sees the device location, live views and recent footage and follows the duress procedure. > Operator contacts authorised responders and records progress without exposing a covert request to the scene unnecessarily. > Supervisor confirms resolution and any device reset is handled separately.
Rules: Never suppress a panic signal due to absent person detection. Distinguish test signals from live signals. Protect covert alarm details and follow site-specific communication restrictions.
Exceptions: Unknown device location still triggers critical review and configuration escalation. Offline cameras do not block response. Duplicate signal delivery must preserve one incident with repeated activations recorded.
Acceptance: A panic event bypasses nuisance filters. A video outage does not delay incident creation. Test mode is unmistakable. An unacknowledged incident reaches the backup operator within the configured deadline.
Scope: Includes visual response support. Excludes replacing the certified source alarm or assuming automatic emergency dispatch authority.
Dependencies: P06 alarm connector; F012 verification; P04 critical routing.
Outputs: Activation record, location, available evidence, acknowledgement and response outcome.

title: Crowd density alerts
Outcome: Warn when estimated occupancy or density in a defined public area exceeds an approved operational threshold.
Inputs: Camera counts, zone geometry, usable area calibration and site capacity policy.
Configure: Choose count or persons-per-area mode, threshold, persistence, hysteresis and responsible crowd-management team. Display estimation limits.
Journey: Installer calibrates the area and validates representative occupancy. > Manager sets the operational threshold and response instructions. > AiWAS shows estimated counts and alerts when the threshold persists. > Operator checks live conditions and coordinates entry control or staff deployment. > The alert clears only after the lower reset threshold persists; operator records the outcome.
Rules: Density requires calibrated usable area; raw image pixels are insufficient. Do not equate an estimate with a certified occupancy count. Overlapping views must be reconciled before aggregation.
Exceptions: Dense occlusion can make counts unreliable. Camera loss shows partial coverage. Furniture or layout changes require recalibration.
Acceptance: Threshold persistence and reset hysteresis work at exact boundaries. Overlapping cameras do not double-count in the approved aggregation method. Unreliable estimates are visibly flagged. A layout change invalidates density calibration.
Scope: Includes awareness and escalation. Excludes a guarantee against crowd crush or autonomous crowd-control actions.
Dependencies: F087 counting; P07 calibration; P04 alerts.
Outputs: Estimated count or density, uncertainty, threshold interval and actions.

title: Sudden crowd movement
Outcome: Surface abrupt crowd dispersal, surges or opposing flow for contextual safety review.
Inputs: Temporal crowd motion, calibrated zones, scene baseline and venue schedule.
Configure: Define supported movement patterns, persistence, expected event phases and response contacts. Validate ordinary departures and celebrations.
