Journey: Venue manager configures normal event phases and monitored areas. > AiWAS detects a candidate motion change and shows the affected region and flow. > Operator checks adjacent cameras and the event context. > Operator coordinates venue staff if conditions warrant intervention. > The episode closes with confirmed crowd issue, expected movement or inconclusive classification.
Rules: Label observable movement rather than panic or fear. Expected end-of-event movement may change thresholds but must not suppress unrelated critical inputs. Correlate related camera observations without assuming every movement has one cause.
Exceptions: Camera vibration, heavy rain, lighting changes and celebrations can resemble abnormal flow. Dense occlusion reduces interpretation. Unknown phase uses the declared fallback policy.
Acceptance: Staged surge examples meet pilot targets. Camera shake is rejected or marked invalid. End-of-event baselines apply only to scheduled periods. Output does not infer emotions.
Scope: Includes movement anomaly candidates. Excludes predicting crowd intent or certifying safe crowd behaviour.
Dependencies: P07 temporal validation; F046 crowd context; P04 incidents.
Outputs: Flow candidate, baseline version, video context and verified response.

title: Evacuation observation
Outcome: Give responders a live view of visible exit use and areas where people are still observed during an evacuation.
Inputs: Explicit evacuation activation, site map, camera coverage, exit counts and optional muster records.
Configure: Define evacuation zones, exits, assembly points, responder roles and alternate views. Mark blind spots and the official all-clear authority.
Journey: Authorised staff activate evacuation mode from an approved signal or manual control. > AiWAS displays exits, visible movement, blocked routes and coverage status. > Operator relays verified observations to responders and records tasks. > Muster or physical sweep results are entered as separate authoritative checks. > The designated human authority ends evacuation mode; the report preserves gaps and decisions.
Rules: No detected people is not proof of an empty building. Video counts and muster records must not be conflated. Do not automatically issue an all-clear or override emergency egress.
Exceptions: Smoke, power loss and network congestion can remove coverage. Re-entry must be visible in the timeline. Partial camera availability remains prominent throughout the incident.
Acceptance: Camera failure marks the affected zone unknown. Evacuation cannot auto-close from a zero count. Physical sweep results remain distinct from AI observations. All-clear records the authorised person.
Scope: Includes observation and coordination. Excludes certified evacuation accounting or automated life-safety control.
Dependencies: F046 or F087; P06 emergency activation; P04 major incidents.
Outputs: Evacuation timeline, observed occupancy, coverage gaps, responder tasks and authorised closure.

title: Entry into dangerous locations
Outcome: Detect a person entering a specifically commissioned hazardous zone and route an appropriate urgent response.
Inputs: Suitable video, hazard geometry, optional equipment or service state and approved safety procedure.
Configure: Define hazard type, boundaries, active periods, warning versus critical zones and required specialist validation. State whether the application is track, water-edge, shaft or machinery monitoring.
Journey: Safety owner approves the hazard-specific scope and tests. > AiWAS observes qualifying entry while the hazard is active. > Operator receives the exact hazard location and available context. > Operator coordinates trained responders under the approved procedure. > Responsible staff confirm the area is safe and document resolution.
Rules: Each hazard is a separate commissioned configuration. Do not infer self-harm intent or medical state. Video software must not directly stop machinery or trains without a separately engineered and approved safety system.
Exceptions: Authorised maintenance, rescuers and changing water levels can alter the scene. Camera occlusion produces loss-of-coverage alarms. Missing equipment state follows the declared conservative policy.
Acceptance: A staged boundary entry creates the correct hazard event. Maintenance overrides expire. Loss of a required state feed is visible. Closing an alert does not assert the physical hazard is removed.
Scope: Includes hazardous-zone observation. Excludes safety-rated interlocks and intent inference.
Dependencies: P07 hazard-specific validation; F003 zones; P06 state optional.
Outputs: Hazard, active state, entry evidence, response actions and authorised resolution.

title: Smoke and flame alerts
Outcome: Add visual smoke or flame candidates through a purpose-built, validated detector or specialist integration.
Inputs: Suitable video or partner detector events, supported smoke/flame classes and fire response procedure.
Configure: Record camera suitability, excluded process areas, persistence and specialist detection limits. Keep statutory alarm-system signals independent.
Journey: Fire-safety owner reviews the intended supplementary use. > Installer commissions the detector using approved test methods and representative nuisance sources. > A candidate produces an urgent alert with source details and surrounding video. > Operator follows the fire procedure and correlates other alarms without waiting for AI certainty. > Authorised personnel resolve the incident and review detector performance.
Rules: A general imagery model is not automatically a compliant fire detector. No visual candidate may suppress a certified fire signal. Do not create unsafe real fires for testing. Preserve detector and model versions.
Exceptions: Steam, dust, welding, sunlight and weather can cause confusion. Smoke outside the camera view is not covered. Feed loss creates a coverage fault, not a normal state.
Acceptance: Approved test sequences trigger under the commissioned settings. Nuisance tests meet the agreed limits. Certified alarm events bypass AI filtering. Detector outage is reported independently.
Scope: Includes supplementary visual alerts. Excludes replacing required fire detection or certifying code compliance.
Dependencies: P06 specialist connector or P07 model; P04 critical routing; F081 health.
Outputs: Smoke/flame candidate, source, evidence, correlated signals and response record.

title: Protective equipment checks
Outcome: Flag apparent absence of a specifically supported item of protective equipment in a zone where it is required.
Inputs: Person detections, validated equipment detector, zone policy, task context and sufficient item visibility.
Configure: Select required equipment by zone and activity; define minimum image quality, observation duration and review routing. Approve helmets, vests and other items individually.
Journey: Safety owner publishes the zone requirement and validates camera suitability. > AiWAS checks visible people against supported required items. > Missing-item candidates enter a safety review queue with the visible body region. > Reviewer distinguishes missing equipment from occlusion or permitted exceptions and assigns corrective action. > Action owner records remediation; aggregate trends show verified events and observation coverage.
Rules: Not visible is different from absent. Wearing an item does not prove fit, certification or correct use. Do not infer an employee identity from a uniform. Use coaching and corrective workflows rather than automatic discipline.
Exceptions: Reflections, colour changes, carried helmets and partially visible bodies need negative tests. Small gloves or eye protection may require dedicated close views. Policy changes are versioned.
Acceptance: Occluded items return unknown. A held helmet does not automatically count as worn. Zone-specific rules apply correctly. Reports distinguish reviewed violations from unreviewed candidates.
Scope: Includes supported visible equipment checks. Excludes certifying all personal protective equipment compliance.
Dependencies: P07 item validation; P03 safety policies; P04 corrective tasks.
Outputs: Required item, observed status, visibility quality, reviewer verdict and corrective action.

title: Forklift pedestrian proximity
Outcome: Find potentially unsafe separation between moving forklifts and pedestrians for safety review.
Inputs: Vehicle and person tracks, calibrated ground plane, vehicle motion and zone policy.
Configure: Set distance, duration, approach direction, low-speed exclusions and physical barrier geometry. Validate scale at multiple scene depths.
Journey: Installer calibrates the monitored junction or aisle. > Safety owner tests representative interactions and approves thresholds. > AiWAS records a candidate proximity event with paths and estimated separation. > Reviewer checks barriers, motion and actual exposure before classifying it. > Corrective actions are assigned and trends reviewed by location and operating period.
Rules: Image-space overlap alone cannot prove physical proximity. Separate near-miss classification from a distance-threshold candidate. Keep distance uncertainty visible. Any real-time warning device requires a separately tested integration.
Exceptions: Racking, guardrails, elevated walkways and occlusion can invalidate distance interpretation. Stationary forklifts may use a different policy. Calibration drift disables numerical distance claims.
Acceptance: Calibrated test distances meet the agreed error bound. A barrier-separated passage follows its exclusion rule. Invalid calibration shows unknown distance. Candidate classification remains reviewable.
Scope: Includes proximity analysis. Excludes safety-rated collision avoidance or guaranteed collision prediction.
Dependencies: P07 geometry validation; P04 safety tasks; F078 motion context.
Outputs: Paths, estimated minimum separation, uncertainty, barriers and corrective outcome.

title: Pedestrian walkway compliance
Outcome: Identify people entering vehicle-only lanes or leaving designated pedestrian paths.
Inputs: Person tracks, walkway and vehicle-lane geometry, operating schedule and temporary route changes.
Configure: Mark permitted paths and crossing points; define prohibited regions, dwell and authorised exceptions.
Journey: Site manager publishes the pedestrian route plan. > Installer tests the geometry against real camera perspective. > AiWAS detects a qualifying route deviation and stores its path. > Reviewer checks whether a diversion, authorised task or actual exposure explains it. > Confirmed issues create corrective tasks and inform route redesign.
Rules: Use the person's ground contact estimate consistently. Crossing at an approved point is allowed. Version routes when barriers or markings change. Do not automatically identify or rank employees.
Exceptions: Temporary closures and deliveries may require alternate routes. A person partly obscured by a vehicle can yield uncertain position. Outdated route geometry must be withdrawn.
Acceptance: Walking wholly inside the approved path creates no event. Entry into the prohibited lane qualifies after persistence. Approved crossing points are excluded. Temporary diversions expire correctly.
Scope: Includes geometric route compliance. Excludes determining fault for an accident.
Dependencies: P03 zone rules; P07 scene commissioning; P04 tasks.
Outputs: Route deviation, policy version, evidence, verified cause and corrective action.

title: Machine exclusion zone entry
Outcome: Correlate person entry into a machine hazard area with the machine's trusted operating state.
Inputs: Person tracks, hazard zones, machine-state connector, state freshness and approved maintenance windows.
Configure: Define hazardous states, state-to-zone mapping, freshness timeout and unknown-state policy. Keep any safety-rated interlock outside this application boundary.
Journey: Safety engineer approves the monitored machine and data source. > Installer validates video geometry and state synchronisation. > AiWAS detects entry while the machine is hazardous or its state is unknown under the configured policy. > Operator or safety reviewer examines the event and follows the site response. > Maintenance or safety staff document resolution and any process change.
Rules: Camera imagery cannot certify lockout. A stale safe state cannot remain safe indefinitely. Store the machine state at event time and its source. AiWAS alerts must not be represented as a certified protective control.
Exceptions: State-feed failure, service mode and authorised entry need distinct handling. Physical guards can block camera visibility. Clock drift may make state correlation uncertain.
Acceptance: Entry during a hazardous state triggers. A stale state becomes unknown after timeout. Maintenance permission does not overwrite the machine-state history. No unsupported stop command is issued.
Scope: Includes state-aware monitoring. Excludes implementing lockout or safety-rated machine stopping.
Dependencies: P06 machine connector; F003 zones; P07 safety validation.
Outputs: Entry interval, machine state and age, authorisation context and response.

title: Blocked emergency exits
Outcome: Detect persistent visible obstructions in the required clearance area of an emergency exit.
Inputs: Camera view, exit-clearance polygon, object observations and clear-scene reference.
Configure: Mark the clearance footprint, permitted transient movement, obstruction persistence and escalation. Link the exit to the building safety plan.
Journey: Safety owner confirms the clearance area on site. > AiWAS observes the region and identifies a persistent object candidate. > Reviewer compares current and clear-reference views and confirms whether access is obstructed. > A removal task goes to responsible staff with a due time. > Staff submit or operator verifies a clear view before resolving the task.
Rules: A visible clear area does not prove the door opens or is unlocked. Passing people should not count as persistent obstruction. Resolved status requires evidence after removal, not only a task button.
Exceptions: Trolleys, deliveries, shadows and seasonal layout changes require tests. Lost view becomes unable to inspect. A new baseline cannot silently accept an existing obstruction.
Acceptance: A placed box beyond persistence produces a candidate. A passing person does not. Baseline updates require review. Closure records a clear-view observation or explicit authorised manual verification.
Scope: Includes visible clearance monitoring. Excludes full fire-egress compliance certification.
Dependencies: P07 scene-change validation; P04 corrective tasks; F018 checks.
Outputs: Exit ID, obstruction duration, evidence, removal task and clearance verification.

title: Blocked safety equipment
Outcome: Detect persistent obstruction of the visible approach area to selected safety equipment.
Inputs: Equipment register, required access footprint, video and approved clear reference.
Configure: Identify each extinguisher, panel or eyewash station and its access zone. Set persistence, allowed temporary work and action owner.
Journey: Safety owner registers the equipment and confirms its required access area. > AiWAS detects a sustained obstruction candidate. > Reviewer checks visibility and whether access is actually impeded. > Responsible staff receive a clearance task with location and evidence. > Reviewer verifies clearance and records repeat causes for follow-up.
Rules: Monitor access, not the equipment's internal condition. Different equipment types need different approved clearance geometry. Keep the original reference and baseline revision history.
Exceptions: The equipment itself may be moved, requiring asset review. A person using the equipment should not be treated as an obstruction by default. Occlusion makes the condition unknown.
Acceptance: Persistent stored goods generate a candidate. A person using an eyewash follows its exclusion policy. Moving the equipment invalidates its old region. Reports distinguish blockage from unavailable view.
Scope: Includes visible access clearance. Excludes checking extinguisher pressure, electrical safety or equipment certification.
Dependencies: P03 asset register; P07 observation validation; P04 tasks.
Outputs: Equipment ID, access obstruction, evidence, corrective owner and clearance result.

title: Lone worker exposure
Outcome: Flag a monitored work activity where visible staffing and approved records do not meet a required buddy rule.
Inputs: Zone occupancy, work permits or task schedule, buddy policy and optional check-in records.
Configure: Define which tasks require two people, qualifying monitored area, persistence and unknown-coverage handling. Avoid applying the rule to every single-person observation.
Journey: Supervisor schedules the task and its staffing requirement. > AiWAS combines active task context with visible occupancy. > A sustained apparent shortfall creates a review task. > Reviewer contacts the supervisor or worker to confirm actual staffing and safety. > Work is paused or corrected under the site procedure; the verified outcome is recorded.
Rules: One visible person does not prove that no colleague is nearby. Coverage must be adequate for the specific buddy rule. Do not infer identity from appearance. A check-in record does not prove continuous physical presence.
Exceptions: Adjacent blind areas, staggered arrivals and temporary departures need explicit rules. Missing task context prevents a definitive policy-breach label.
Acceptance: An active two-person task with one visible worker creates a candidate after persistence. An unrelated one-person task does not. Coverage loss marks the count unknown. Human confirmation is captured before final classification.
Scope: Includes staffing-rule review. Excludes guaranteeing lone-worker protection or replacing personal distress devices.
Dependencies: F087 counts; P06 work permits; P04 welfare tasks.
Outputs: Task requirement, observed count, coverage, contact attempt and verified staffing outcome.

title: Loading dock hazards
Outcome: Surface defined visible loading-dock exposures such as a person near an unprotected edge or moving vehicle path.
Inputs: Dock geometry, person and vehicle tracks, trailer presence and optional dock equipment state.
Configure: Define edge zones, loading states, safe waiting areas and supported hazard types. Validate each hazard rather than enabling a general unsafe dock label.
Journey: Safety owner maps the dock and approved operating conditions. > AiWAS correlates visible activity with the selected dock state. > A qualifying exposure creates a clip with the exact rule reason. > Reviewer checks trailer position, barriers and task context. > Responsible staff act and document the correction or explained condition.
Rules: Camera-only trailer presence does not certify that restraints or dock levellers are safe. State-dependent rules require fresh signals. Link simultaneous proximity and edge events into one reviewable episode.
Exceptions: Open trailer doors, shadows and partial vehicle views can confuse state. Dock layout changes require recalibration. Missing restraint data remains unknown.
Acceptance: A staged edge-zone entry triggers under the relevant state. A safe waiting area is excluded. Stale dock state is visible. Reports never claim a vehicle restraint is engaged from mere trailer presence.
Scope: Includes specified visible exposures. Excludes certifying dock equipment or controlling restraints.
Dependencies: P07 dock validation; P06 state optional; F052 proximity.
Outputs: Dock hazard type, state evidence, trajectories and corrective action.

title: Work at height exceptions
Outcome: Surface specific visible exceptions involving ladders, guardrails or supported fall-protection observations.
Inputs: Suitable views, approved work zone, task permit and validated equipment or posture models.
Configure: Define supported observations separately, such as ladder use in a prohibited region or a visible missing guardrail. Record the visibility limits of harness and anchor inspection.
Journey: Safety owner selects a narrow use case and validates sample footage. > AiWAS identifies a candidate exception during active work. > Reviewer inspects the full context and checks the permit or competent-person assessment. > The site team responds through its work-at-height procedure. > Corrective action and verification are attached to the event.
Rules: A visible harness is not proof of correct attachment. Do not infer a safe anchor from an indistinct line. AI findings are screening observations requiring competent review.
Exceptions: Occluded anchors, complex scaffolding and lifted platforms may be unsupported. Movement of ladders or temporary structures requires updated geometry. Insufficient view must return unknown.
Acceptance: Supported staged exceptions meet the pilot criteria. An invisible anchor is reported unknown. A permit cannot automatically certify observed equipment condition. Each event names the narrow observation it supports.
Scope: Includes validated visible exceptions. Excludes full work-at-height compliance certification or fall arrest control.
Dependencies: P07 specialist validation; P06 permits optional; P04 corrective tasks.
Outputs: Specific observed exception, visibility limits, permit context and competent review.

title: Unsafe posture and manual handling
Outcome: Screen visible lifting or repetitive postures to prioritise ergonomic assessment of work processes.
Inputs: Suitable full-body video, calibrated pose estimates, task context and approved assessment method.
Configure: Define supported movements, observation windows, minimum pose quality and aggregation periods. Set whether findings are task-level only; default to no individual ranking.
Journey: Ergonomics owner selects a task and approves observation conditions. > AiWAS extracts candidate posture intervals and summarises frequency. > Qualified reviewer examines examples and the method's limitations. > Reviewer assigns a process improvement or further assessment. > Follow-up observations compare the task under similar coverage and conditions.
Rules: Body posture alone cannot measure load weight, force, pain or injury. Any assessment score must identify its method and unobserved inputs. Do not diagnose musculoskeletal conditions or rank employee health.
Exceptions: Occlusion, loose clothing, seated tasks and perspective can invalidate pose estimates. A changed task or camera invalidates direct before-and-after comparison.
Acceptance: Low-quality poses are excluded and counted as missing coverage. Unobserved force is not fabricated. Reports aggregate by approved task. Comparison periods disclose differences in observation coverage.
Scope: Includes ergonomic screening. Excludes medical diagnosis and automatic worker performance decisions.
Dependencies: P07 pose validation; P09 aggregation; P04 corrective tasks.
Outputs: Candidate postures, task frequency, method limitations and reviewer recommendations.

title: Possible concealment gestures
Outcome: Surface supported merchandise-handling gestures for contextual loss-prevention review.
Inputs: Suitable aisle video, temporal gesture model, product zones and retailer response policy.
Configure: Enable only validated gesture classes and camera views; set sequence duration, threshold and authorised reviewers. Test normal bag use, phones and shopping behaviour.
Journey: Retail manager validates the deployment and staff response process. > AiWAS detects a candidate hand-to-bag or hand-to-clothing sequence near merchandise. > Reviewer watches the full sequence, including any visible item interaction. > Staff act only under the retailer's approved procedure and supporting evidence. > Reviewer records relevant, explained or inconclusive with no automatic theft label.
Rules: A gesture does not establish non-payment, ownership or intent. Do not generate offender profiles or identify repeat offenders from appearance. Preserve context before and after the candidate.
Exceptions: Reusable bags, personal belongings and occluded hands can produce ambiguity. Crowded shelves may be unsuitable. No visible item means the system must not invent one.
Acceptance: Candidate clips include the action context. Negative shopping examples meet the pilot limit. The UI never automatically states theft confirmed. Reviewers can classify uncertainty without forcing a binary accusation.
Scope: Includes gesture candidates. Excludes automatic detention, accusation or cross-store person watchlists.
Dependencies: P07 gesture validation; P08 restricted evidence; P04 review.
Outputs: Gesture type, clip, visibility, reviewer decision and any authorised action.

title: Rapid shelf clearing
Outcome: Detect unusually rapid visible removal of multiple items from a configured shelf area.
Inputs: Shelf video, product-region geometry, removal observations and optional replenishment schedule.
Configure: Set minimum supported removal count or scene-change magnitude, time window and stock-replenishment exceptions. State whether exact item counting is validated.
Journey: Manager marks the shelf and tests ordinary shopping and replenishment. > AiWAS observes a burst of removals and opens a candidate. > Reviewer checks the sequence and whether staff restocking or a legitimate bulk purchase explains it. > Store staff follow the approved response policy. > Reviewer records the outcome and any shelf or staffing change.
Rules: Use an approximate-removal label unless item-level counting is validated. Do not equate rapid removal with theft. A replenishment exception must be time-bound and auditable.
Exceptions: Promotional displays, reflections and shelf rearrangement affect the baseline. Multiple shoppers may act simultaneously. Empty or moved shelves require recommissioning.
Acceptance: Validated bulk-removal clips generate a candidate. Slow ordinary removal below the configured threshold does not. Replenishment policy applies only during its window. Unvalidated counts are not shown as exact.
Scope: Includes rapid visible activity. Excludes inventory accuracy or intent determination.
Dependencies: P07 shelf validation; P03 exceptions; P04 review.
Outputs: Shelf region, time window, estimated removals or change score and verdict.

title: Checkout scan exceptions
Outcome: Compare visible item passage through a checkout with transaction records to identify possible scan discrepancies.
Inputs: Checkout video, scan and transaction events, till identity, clock alignment and validated item-passage observations.
Configure: Map each camera to its till; set matching windows, multi-buy treatment and cashier-assisted correction workflow. Define supported checkout layouts.
Journey: Installer validates item passage and transaction synchronisation. > AiWAS compares observed passages with scans during an open transaction. > A mismatch creates a candidate showing video and matched or missing scan records. > Reviewer checks quantities, rescans, produce weighing and transaction completion. > Staff correct or document the exception under retailer policy; final outcome updates the review record.
Rules: Do not infer product SKU or price unless a validated source supports it. A pending scan may resolve a provisional exception. Transaction voids and quantities require explicit reconciliation logic.
Exceptions: Stacked goods, bags, weighted produce and scan-feed delays can make matching uncertain. Feed outage pauses definitive mismatch labels. Customer-facing interventions require a separately approved design.
Acceptance: Delayed valid scans reconcile within the matching window. Quantity entries cover their declared item count. Feed loss returns unknown. Every candidate links to the exact till and transaction.
Scope: Includes review-oriented reconciliation. Excludes automatic theft accusation or unapproved checkout interruption.
Dependencies: P06 point-of-sale connector; P07 passage validation; P04 review.
Outputs: Transaction match set, candidate discrepancy, timing uncertainty and resolved outcome.

title: Refund void and till event review
Outcome: Retrieve relevant footage for selected transaction exceptions so reviewers can assess the actual activity.
Inputs: Refunds, voids, cash-drawer openings or other approved transaction events and mapped checkout cameras.
Configure: Select event types, amount thresholds if applicable, video padding, review sampling and authorised roles.
Journey: Manager connects the transaction feed and confirms camera mapping. > A qualifying till event creates a review item. > AiWAS retrieves the related clip and displays the source transaction facts. > Reviewer checks the activity and supporting business records, then records a factual conclusion. > Confirmed process issues route to the appropriate manager; evidence access remains restricted.
Rules: A refund or void is not inherently suspicious. Keep source transaction values immutable. Review outcomes must distinguish ordinary processing, process exception, missing evidence and unresolved concern.
Exceptions: Shared tills, clock drift and offline transaction posting can misalign footage. Cancelled or corrected transactions retain their history. Sensitive payment details must be minimised.
Acceptance: A qualifying test event retrieves the correct till interval. Corrected transactions remain linked. Unauthorised users cannot view transaction details. Missing footage is explicit rather than interpreted adversely.
Scope: Includes transaction-linked review. Excludes automatic employee fraud scoring or payment-card data storage.
Dependencies: P06 point-of-sale events; F012 retrieval pattern; P08 evidence.
Outputs: Transaction reference, clip, reviewer classification and follow-up task.

title: Stockroom movement exceptions
Outcome: Compare visible movement of goods through controlled stockroom points with approved transfer records.
Inputs: Video at transfer points, supported object observations, warehouse transfers and operating windows.
Configure: Define movement points, direction, supported goods classes and matching rules. Use barcode or RFID records when item identity is required.
Journey: Warehouse manager maps the transfer process and records. > AiWAS observes a qualifying goods movement. > The system seeks an approved transfer and shows matched, unmatched or uncertain status. > Reviewer checks the clip and source records with warehouse staff. > Missing paperwork or a verified exception is resolved and the final match retained.
Rules: A box on video is not a known SKU. Aggregate counts require a validated view. Late paperwork creates provisional exceptions rather than immediate misconduct findings.
Exceptions: Empty pallets, nested containers and occlusion affect counts. Connector outage stops definitive reconciliation. Authorised urgent transfers require an audited manual reference.
Acceptance: A matching approved transfer resolves the observation. An unmatched movement opens a review task after the grace window. Barcode identity is never invented from a generic box image. Feed failure shows unknown.
Scope: Includes transfer exceptions. Excludes complete inventory control or proof of theft.
Dependencies: P06 warehouse records; P07 object validation; P04 review.
Outputs: Observed movement, transfer match, count quality and reconciliation outcome.

title: High value display interaction
Outcome: Flag defined interactions with a protected display, case or cage outside approved operating conditions.
Inputs: Display camera, interaction region, supported action detector and optional lock or service state.
Configure: Define supported triggers such as prolonged handling or reaching into a closed-hours region. Link authorised service periods and case-open sensors where available.
Journey: Manager registers the display and permitted interactions. > AiWAS detects a qualifying candidate with surrounding context. > Reviewer checks whether staff service, a sale or an unexplained interaction is occurring. > Store staff receive a response task under the approved procedure. > The outcome and any equipment issue are documented.
Rules: Physical lock state comes from a trusted sensor, not appearance alone. Different displays require scene-specific validation. Do not describe an interaction as attempted theft automatically.
Exceptions: Reflections in glass, crowds and staff demonstrations can confuse detections. Display relocation invalidates geometry. An unknown service state must remain visible.
Acceptance: A staged configured interaction creates a candidate. Approved service windows apply correctly. Reflections meet pilot false-alert limits. Every event names the specific interaction rule.
Scope: Includes supported display interactions. Excludes hidden tamper detection or intent inference.
Dependencies: P07 interaction validation; P06 state optional; F009 assets.
Outputs: Display ID, candidate interaction, service context, clip and review result.

title: Asset removal through exits
Outcome: Flag a designated visible asset or supported asset class crossing an exit from a controlled area.
Inputs: Asset register or validated object class, exit geometry, trajectories and optional removal permits.
Configure: Define what can be recognised, outbound direction, approved removal windows and review owner. Use tags or barcode records for unique identity where needed.
Journey: Manager registers the asset class and exit policy. > Installer validates carried, wheeled and partly hidden examples. > AiWAS detects an outbound movement and retrieves any matching permit. > Operator verifies the object and checks with the responsible team. > Approved removal or an actual exception is recorded with the supporting permit or response.
Rules: Similar appearance is not unique asset identity. Do not infer ownership. Require an outbound crossing, not presence near the exit. Preserve the permit status at event time.
Exceptions: Packaging, carts and occlusion may hide the asset. Multiple identical items need external identifiers. Emergency removal follows a documented override.
Acceptance: A supported outbound asset creates a candidate. Inbound movement does not. Missing unique identity is labelled class-only. An expired permit does not approve a new removal.
Scope: Includes visible asset movement. Excludes full asset tracking through blind areas or automatic accusations.
Dependencies: F002 crossing; P07 asset recognition; P06 permits optional.
Outputs: Asset candidate, direction, permit context, evidence and final disposition.

title: Parcel handover and collection
Outcome: Maintain evidence of parcel arrival, authorised collection and unresolved parcel removals.
Inputs: Parcel intake record or code, drop-off camera, collection authorisation and optional locker events.
Configure: Map parcel zones and collection points; define authorised staff roles, retention and recipient verification procedure.
Journey: Staff register a delivered parcel using a code or manual reference. > AiWAS links the intake time to video and stores the parcel location. > Recipient requests collection and staff verify entitlement through the approved process. > Collection records link to video or locker events; an unexplained disappearance becomes a review task. > Staff close the parcel record and handle disputes with controlled evidence access.
Rules: Video appearance alone cannot prove parcel contents or recipient entitlement. A tracking code is the identity anchor. Avoid exposing other residents' or customers' parcel details.
Exceptions: Multiple parcels in one bag, moved storage locations and failed locker updates require reconciliation. A missing parcel observation is not proof of theft.
Acceptance: Collection requires the configured authorisation. A parcel move preserves location history. Disappearance without collection produces a task. A recipient cannot access other parcel records or footage.
Scope: Includes handover evidence and record management. Excludes carrier tracking or content verification unless integrated.
Dependencies: P06 parcel or locker records; F036 change search; P08 evidence.
Outputs: Parcel lifecycle, handover references, collection authorisation and dispute evidence.

title: Equipment or kiosk tampering
Outcome: Surface defined visible interference with a protected kiosk, terminal, camera or other asset.
Inputs: Asset view, interaction model or scene-change rule, service windows and optional tamper sensor.
Configure: Select narrow triggers such as persistent covering, unusual cabinet interaction or an attached-object change. Record supported resolution and viewpoint.
Journey: Asset owner approves the monitored interaction and baseline. > AiWAS detects a candidate or correlates a tamper sensor. > Operator reviews the scene, maintenance schedule and device health. > Operator contacts the site team or maintenance provider. > Confirmed tampering, authorised service or a faulty sensor is documented with evidence.
Rules: A changed appearance does not establish a skimmer or malicious device. Trusted physical tamper signals remain distinct from visual inference. Baseline changes require approval.
Exceptions: Cleaning, repairs, decals and reflections can cause candidates. A covered camera may lose the ability to observe the person responsible. Do not collect PIN entry or payment-screen content unnecessarily.
Acceptance: A validated covering or interaction test creates a candidate. Authorised service is traceable. The UI does not identify a skimmer without supporting inspection. Baseline replacement preserves history.
Scope: Includes supported visible interference. Excludes detecting hidden electronics or payment fraud from general footage.
Dependencies: F081 health; P07 interaction validation; P06 tamper signals optional.
Outputs: Asset, observed change, source signal, service context and verified finding.

title: Delivery discrepancy review
Outcome: Assemble delivery footage and shipment records to investigate shortages, damage or disputed handovers.
Inputs: Shipment ID, gate and bay times, delivery records, relevant cameras and staff notes.
Configure: Map shipment milestones to cameras; define retrieval windows, document access and evidence-retention rules.
Journey: User opens a shipment dispute and enters the shipment reference. > AiWAS retrieves gate, unloading and handover intervals with source records. > Investigator reviews what is visibly countable and compares paperwork. > Staff add factual notes and identify missing evidence or conflicting records. > Investigator approves a report and controlled evidence package for the dispute.
Rules: Distinguish visible package count from verified contents. Do not infer pre-existing damage where no arrival view exists. Keep original delivery records and later corrections separate.
Exceptions: Pallet wrapping and off-camera unloading may prevent exact counts. Multiple shipments in one vehicle require bay and time disambiguation. Gaps must remain visible in conclusions.
Acceptance: A shipment reference retrieves the correct bay interval. Ambiguous overlapping deliveries require selection. Reported counts state their observation basis. Missing arrival footage prevents an unsupported before-and-after claim.
Scope: Includes evidence-supported review. Excludes automatic liability allocation or inventory certification.
Dependencies: P06 shipment records; F037 timeline; F039 evidence export.
Outputs: Shipment timeline, visible observations, discrepancies, limitations and approved report.

title: Vehicle arrival and departure logs
Outcome: Maintain searchable vehicle passage records with plate-read confidence and original entrance evidence.
Inputs: Suitable plate camera or recognition service, lane direction, capture time and vehicle image.
Configure: Set country or plate-format support, lane mapping, duplicate-read interval, retention and correction permissions. Validate day, night and expected speeds.
Journey: Installer commissions each lane and tests representative plates. > AiWAS groups repeated reads into a passage and stores the original text and image. > Gate operator reviews uncertain reads or corrects a transcription with a reason. > Authorised users search arrivals and departures by plate, lane or period. > Reports show passage history and any unmatched entry or exit for review.
Rules: Normalise formatting for matching but preserve raw text. Plate reads identify a displayed plate, not a verified owner or driver. A manual correction creates a revision. Do not merge separate passages solely because plates match.
Exceptions: Dirty, obscured, temporary and unsupported plates can be unreadable. A missed exit leaves an unresolved visit, not guaranteed continued presence. Motorcycle and trailer plates need lane-specific validation.
Acceptance: Repeated frames yield one passage. A corrected read retains its original value. Unreadable plates remain searchable by time and image. Separate visits are not collapsed.
Scope: Includes site passage logging. Excludes ownership databases and public-road movement tracking.
Dependencies: P06 recognition or P07 OCR validation; P08 retention; P09 search.
Outputs: Passage ID, raw and normalised read, confidence, image, direction and corrections.

title: Approved vehicle access
Outcome: Use a plate observation as one input to an approved gate-access policy.
Inputs: Plate passage, current authorisation list, access schedule, gate controller and safety interlocks.
Configure: Define confidence threshold, valid lanes and times, manual fallback and whether release is operator-approved or policy-automated. Initial release defaults to operator-approved release.
Journey: Manager registers a vehicle authorisation with expiry. > A vehicle arrives and AiWAS compares the read with current permissions. > Gate operator sees match, unknown or denied and supporting evidence. > Authorised release sends an expiring idempotent command through the controller. > Passage and gate acknowledgement are logged; uncertain outcomes are reconciled before retry.
Rules: A plate match is not proof of driver identity. Controller interlocks remain authoritative. Revoked or stale permissions cannot silently grant entry. High-security sites can require another credential.
Exceptions: Low-confidence reads go to manual review. Network loss follows the site's controller fallback policy. Plate cloning is outside camera-only verification.
Acceptance: Expired authorisation cannot release the gate. Duplicate commands do not create repeated openings. Low-confidence reads do not auto-admit. Unknown command outcome triggers status checking rather than blind retry.
Scope: Includes permission-based gate workflow. Excludes bypassing safety interlocks or proving vehicle ownership.
Dependencies: F071 plate logs; P06 controller; P01 command permissions.
Outputs: Access decision, policy version, authorisation, command status and passage record.

title: Site specific vehicle alerts
Outcome: Notify authorised staff when a plate matches a current site-specific operational list.
Inputs: Plate reads, approved list entries, purpose, validity interval and response instructions.
Configure: Require list owner, lawful purpose, site scope, expiry and review cadence. Distinguish expected delivery, service vehicle and restricted-access lists.
Journey: Authorised manager adds an entry with justification and expiry. > AiWAS checks incoming plate observations against active entries. > Operator receives a potential match with read confidence and the approved action. > Operator verifies the image before acting on a consequential match. > The action and any list correction are recorded; expired entries stop matching.
Rules: No cross-client list sharing by default. Preserve false-match corrections. A list entry must not automatically imply criminal status. Do not add plates from unrelated footage without a defined authorised purpose.
Exceptions: Similar characters and cloned plates can cause false matches. Low-confidence recognition needs verification. List-feed failure must display freshness and follow the configured policy.
Acceptance: An expired entry produces no new list alert. A plate from another customer cannot match. A low-confidence read shows potential match. Every entry has an owner, purpose and expiry.
Scope: Includes bounded site lists. Excludes unrestricted vehicle surveillance or unverified criminal labelling.
Dependencies: F071; P01 list governance; P03 validity rules.
Outputs: List match, entry purpose, confidence, verification and action audit.

title: Parking occupancy
Outcome: Estimate occupied and available parking bays or zone capacity from suitable camera views.
Inputs: Parking video, bay geometry or validated zone counts and current layout.
Configure: Mark bays, excluded spaces, occupancy persistence and unknown-state timeout. Specify bay-based versus aggregate mode.
Journey: Installer maps and tests each bay or counting zone. > AiWAS updates occupied, available or unknown state as vehicles move. > Parking operator views availability and coverage on the site map. > Operator corrects geometry or records temporary closures. > Reports summarise occupancy and duration with missing-coverage intervals disclosed.
Rules: Occluded bays must not be labelled available. Temporary closures reduce usable capacity separately from occupancy. Two cameras viewing one bay share one authoritative state calculation.
Exceptions: Motorcycles, oversize vehicles and parking across lines need explicit policies. Snow, glare or moved cameras can invalidate observations. Stale data is visibly aged.
Acceptance: A validated arrival changes the bay to occupied after persistence. Camera loss changes affected bays to unknown. Closed bays are excluded from available capacity. Duplicate views do not double-count.
Scope: Includes availability estimation. Excludes legal enforcement and guaranteed reservation fulfilment.
Dependencies: P07 bay validation; P09 dashboards; F081 health.
Outputs: Bay or zone state, confidence, last observation, capacity and occupancy history.

title: Parking violations
Outcome: Identify possible breaches of site parking rules for human review.
Inputs: Vehicle position and duration, parking zones, permits, operating hours and site policy.
Configure: Define overstays, loading restrictions, reserved spaces and fire-lane rules with grace periods and exceptions. Set reviewer and permitted response actions.
Journey: Manager publishes the parking policy and permit source. > AiWAS observes parking and maintains a qualified duration record. > A possible breach opens a task with the applicable rule and permit status. > Reviewer checks evidence, timing and exceptions before contacting the driver or site team. > Resolution records departure, valid permission or an approved enforcement referral.
Rules: A missing permit feed is unknown, not no permit. Duration requires reliable passage or occupancy continuity. Any fine or towing process is outside the initial automated scope.
Exceptions: Deliveries, emergency vehicles, inaccessible permits and missed departure observations need review. Public-road rules must not be assumed from site settings.
Acceptance: An overstay starts only after the configured grace period. A valid permit resolves the candidate. Feed loss prevents definitive no-permit classification. A recording gap is disclosed in duration evidence.
Scope: Includes site-policy candidates. Excludes automatic fines, towing orders or legal determinations.
Dependencies: F071 or F074; P06 permits; P04 tasks.
Outputs: Rule, observed interval, permit context, reviewer verdict and resolution.

title: Vehicle queues and dwell times
Outcome: Measure waiting and service times at gates, checkpoints or loading zones.
Inputs: Vehicle tracks, queue entry and service boundaries, lane geometry and coverage.
Configure: Define queue start, service start and departure events; set queue-length and waiting-time thresholds. Specify whether tracking across cameras is validated.
Journey: Manager maps the process and tests a sample vehicle journey. > AiWAS timestamps entry, service and departure observations. > Dashboard shows current queue estimates and long-wait candidates. > Operator opens the relevant view and allocates staff or a bay if needed. > Completed intervals feed aggregate reports with incomplete journeys separated.
Rules: Waiting time and service time are different metrics. Lost tracks produce censored or incomplete intervals rather than invented departure times. Shared lanes need a declared association method.
Exceptions: Vehicles leaving and rejoining, overtaking or parking nearby can confuse continuity. Camera outages invalidate affected measurement periods.
Acceptance: A labelled test journey calculates waiting and service durations separately. A lost track is not reported as completed service. Threshold alerts use persistence. Reports disclose incomplete journeys.
Scope: Includes operational measurements. Excludes guaranteed driver identification or inferred delivery completion.
Dependencies: P02 trajectories; P09 aggregation; P07 measurement validation.
Outputs: Queue length, waiting and service intervals, coverage and intervention record.

title: Stopped vehicles and obstructions
Outcome: Flag a vehicle remaining stationary in a configured circulation or access lane beyond the permitted interval.
Inputs: Vehicle tracks, lane polygon, motion estimate, stop duration and permitted-stop zones.
Configure: Define monitored lanes, stop threshold, traffic-signal or queue context and response instructions.
Journey: Site manager tests normal traffic and authorised stopping. > AiWAS detects a stationary vehicle within a protected lane and starts a timer. > A sustained stop creates an alert with duration and surrounding traffic. > Operator determines whether it is congestion, breakdown, loading or an obstruction requiring action. > Staff resolve the issue; the incident records movement resumption and human outcome.
Rules: A stopped vehicle is not automatically a crash. Normal queue zones should use separate thresholds or F076 context. Confirm stationary state over time rather than a single frame.
Exceptions: Congestion, traffic lights and loading can explain stops. Camera shake can mimic motion. A hidden vehicle may be unobservable rather than departed.
Acceptance: A stop beyond threshold triggers once. A permitted loading zone does not. Queue-context policy applies correctly. Loss of visibility does not falsely record clearance.
Scope: Includes configured stationary-vehicle alerts. Excludes automatic incident causation or road enforcement.
Dependencies: P03 rules; F076 context optional; P04 incidents.
Outputs: Vehicle location, stop duration, context, verified cause and clearance.

title: Site speed and near miss review
Outcome: Estimate site vehicle speed and surface possible conflict events for safety analysis.
Inputs: Calibrated trajectories or radar speed, timebase, lane geometry and person or vehicle paths.
Configure: Record measurement method, error limits, site speed policy and supported conflict definitions. Use separate thresholds for speed and proximity candidates.
Journey: Installer validates speed against a trusted reference at several positions. > AiWAS calculates supported measurements and flags threshold candidates. > Reviewer inspects trajectories, uncertainty and relevant footage. > Verified operational concerns create corrective tasks or training actions. > Periodic recalibration and sampling maintain measurement quality.
Rules: Uncalibrated image displacement cannot be labelled kilometres per hour. A near miss is a reviewed classification, not every close path. Do not use estimates as enforcement-grade evidence without a separately qualified system.
Exceptions: Perspective, turning, occlusion and frame-rate variation affect estimates. Radar association can attach to the wrong vehicle if not validated. Calibration expiry disables numerical claims.
Acceptance: Reference runs meet the approved error tolerance. Expired calibration blocks speed values. Two nearby vehicles retain distinct measurements. Candidate conflict labels require reviewer confirmation.
Scope: Includes safety analysis. Excludes certified speeding enforcement or collision prediction guarantees.
Dependencies: P07 calibration; P06 radar optional; F052 proximity.
Outputs: Measurement method, speed or conflict candidate, uncertainty and verified action.

title: Loading bay assignment checks
Outcome: Compare a vehicle observed at a loading bay with the planned appointment and allocation.
Inputs: Bay occupancy, plate or trailer identifier, appointment system, assignment updates and bay map.
Configure: Map camera views to bays; define identifier source, early/late windows and reassignment permissions.
Journey: Planner allocates the appointment to a bay. > AiWAS observes the arriving vehicle or trailer and retrieves the active allocation. > Correct matches update arrival status; mismatches create a review task. > Operator verifies the identifier and directs the vehicle or approves a reassignment. > Departure closes the bay visit and preserves the original and revised allocation.
Rules: Generic vehicle appearance is insufficient for unique appointment matching. Reassignment requires an authorised planner or operator. Trailer swaps must be explicit linked events. Feed freshness is visible.
Exceptions: Unreadable plates, shared tractor units and last-minute changes can create ambiguity. Offline scheduling uses manual verification rather than assumed allocation.
Acceptance: Correct identifiers match the allocated bay. A wrong bay creates a task. Reassignment records approver and history. Unreadable identifiers remain unmatched rather than guessed.
Scope: Includes assignment verification. Excludes confirming cargo contents or loading completion from occupancy alone.
Dependencies: F071 identifiers; F074 occupancy pattern; P06 appointment records.
Outputs: Bay visit, observed identifier, appointment match, reassignment and departure.

title: Vehicle damage event review
Outcome: Preserve and organise footage around a possible vehicle impact or reported damage event.
Inputs: Reported vehicle and time, candidate impact observations, camera views and optional arrival/departure images.
Configure: Define supported impact candidates, evidence windows and review roles. Separate impact detection from visible before-and-after inspection.
Journey: A user reports damage or AiWAS surfaces a possible impact. > Investigator selects the vehicle, location and approximate interval. > AiWAS assembles relevant clips and any comparable before-and-after views. > Investigator verifies visible contact and documents what damage is actually observable. > An approved evidence package supports the customer's dispute process.
Rules: Contact does not prove damage and damage does not prove who caused it. Comparisons require sufficiently similar views and quality. Preserve missing angles and pre-existing uncertainty.
Exceptions: Reflections, occlusion and minor impacts can be undetectable. A vehicle arriving already damaged cannot be assessed without a usable arrival view. Reported time may need a wider search.
Acceptance: A reported interval retrieves correct cameras. Missing before imagery is disclosed. Candidate impact is not automatically labelled proven damage. Export retains originals and annotations separately.
Scope: Includes candidate detection and evidence review. Excludes automated insurance liability decisions.
Dependencies: F033 search; F037 timeline; F039 evidence; P07 impact pilot optional.
Outputs: Impact candidates, comparison views, factual findings, limitations and evidence package.

title: Camera image health monitoring
Outcome: Detect loss of usable camera imagery and create a maintenance task before coverage is assumed available.
Inputs: Video frames, approved scene baseline, image-quality measurements and camera maintenance state.
Configure: Set supported fault types, persistence, expected day/night changes and approved maintenance windows. Record baseline owner and camera purpose.
Journey: Installer captures a usable baseline and tests covering, blur and redirection. > AiWAS compares current imagery with the baseline and quality limits. > A sustained fault creates a task and marks dependent rules degraded. > Maintenance operator inspects the view, diagnoses the cause and repairs or repositions the camera. > A valid recovery test clears the fault; baseline changes require approval.
Rules: Distinguish blocked, blurred, redirected and underexposed where supported. Healthy stream availability does not imply usable imagery. Do not automatically learn a blocked view as the new normal.
Exceptions: Darkness, weather, seasonal changes and scheduled PTZ movement can be expected or faults depending on the profile. A camera redirect may be intentional but still invalidate zone geometry.
Acceptance: A sustained cover creates a fault. Stream connectivity alone does not clear it. Baseline replacement is audited. Dependent geometry rules are flagged after redirection.
Scope: Includes image usability. Excludes proving deliberate tampering or guaranteeing camera coverage.
Dependencies: P02 video; P03 baseline versioning; P04 maintenance tasks.
Outputs: Fault type, onset, affected rules, repair history and verified recovery.

title: Recording and stream availability
Outcome: Detect missing streams, archive gaps and stale device telemetry with separate coverage states.
Inputs: Stream heartbeats, recorder status, sampled archive retrieval, device health and expected operating schedule.
Configure: Set stale thresholds, archive-check frequency, expected retention, maintenance windows and escalation. Define separate live, recording and analytics health.
Journey: Administrator connects the recorder and sets coverage expectations. > AiWAS checks live ingestion and verifies sample recordings at scheduled intervals. > A fault opens a maintenance task and annotates affected coverage periods. > Operator investigates network, recorder, storage or authentication causes. > Recovery checks confirm live and archive service independently before closing.
Rules: A live camera can have failed recording. A recorder's healthy response does not prove retrievable footage; sample retrieval is required. Never fill archive gaps with repeated frames without explicit labelling.
Exceptions: Planned downtime, credential expiry and full storage need distinct reasons. Late backfill may restore archive coverage but does not erase the original outage.
Acceptance: Live video with failed recording produces an archive fault. Stale telemetry becomes unknown. Successful backfill updates coverage with history. A failed test retrieval prevents a healthy-archive claim.
Scope: Includes availability verification. Excludes recorder repair or guaranteed recovery of lost footage.
Dependencies: P06 recorder connector; P02 coverage registry; P04 maintenance.
Outputs: Live, archive and analytics status, gap intervals, fault cause and recovery evidence.

title: Guard post coverage
Outcome: Flag an apparently unattended guard post during a scheduled staffing obligation.
Inputs: Post schedule, authorised breaks or relief, designated post view and person-presence observations.
Configure: Define post region, required coverage periods, absence grace and relief procedure. Avoid identity inference or automatic employee performance scores.
Journey: Supervisor publishes the staffing and relief schedule. > AiWAS observes presence in the designated post during required periods. > Sustained apparent absence creates a supervisor task. > Supervisor checks relief, patrol assignment or emergency work before classifying a coverage gap. > Staffing is restored or the schedule corrected; the verified explanation is recorded.
Rules: Someone present is not proof that the assigned guard is present. A camera cannot establish attentiveness or competence. Do not treat a blind spot as absence. Duty changes must be auditable.
Exceptions: Breaks, response duties and obscured views can explain missing observation. A public person entering the post area may not fulfil staffing. Check-in records require separate corroboration.
Acceptance: Scheduled relief suppresses only its approved interval. Camera outage shows unknown coverage. Presence is not assigned automatically to a named employee. Confirmed gaps require supervisor review.
Scope: Includes staffing coverage review. Excludes emotion, fatigue or productivity inference from appearance.
Dependencies: P06 roster; P03 schedules; P04 supervisor tasks.
Outputs: Required period, observed presence, uncertainty, supervisor finding and staffing action.

title: Patrol completion verification
Outcome: Correlate submitted patrol checkpoints with available site evidence and identify discrepancies for review.
Inputs: Patrol runs, checkpoint scans, guard logs, mapped camera intervals and optional on-duty location.
Configure: Define checkpoint evidence requirements, matching windows and what counts as verified, self-reported or unable to verify.
Journey: Guard completes a checkpoint through the patrol system. > AiWAS retrieves the mapped evidence and compares timing. > Supervisor reviews matches and discrepancies in the patrol run. > Guard or supervisor supplies an explanation for missing or conflicting evidence. > The run closes with a verification status for each checkpoint and any follow-up task.
Rules: Seeing a person near a checkpoint does not prove every inspection action occurred. Preserve guard-submitted data unchanged. Missing camera evidence is not automatically a false report.
Exceptions: Camera outages, shared routes, delayed mobile sync and emergency diversions need explicit classifications. One clip cannot verify checkpoints outside its visible scope.
Acceptance: A matching checkpoint links to the correct interval. Offline submissions preserve event and receipt times. Missing evidence is unable to verify. A supervisor correction retains the original claim.
Scope: Includes evidence correlation. Excludes automatic misconduct findings or continuous off-duty tracking.
Dependencies: F011 patrol runs; P06 guard system; P08 evidence.
Outputs: Checkpoint claim, verification level, evidence, discrepancies and supervisor resolution.

title: Response time measurement
Outcome: Measure incident handling and guard response using explicit workflow timestamps and agreed service rules.
Inputs: Event occurrence and receipt, incident creation, acknowledgement, verification, assignment, acceptance, arrival and closure.
Configure: Define each metric's start/end events, business calendar, permitted pauses and exclusions. Version the customer service-level policy.
Journey: Supervisor selects the reporting period and applicable service policy. > AiWAS computes durations from immutable status events. > Dashboard highlights breaches, missing milestones and incomplete incidents. > Supervisor investigates causes and records approved corrections without replacing raw times. > Customer reports show the metric definition, coverage and relevant exceptions.
Rules: Separate detection delay from operator handling and travel time. Missing arrival is not zero travel time. Pauses need a permitted reason and cannot silently erase an earlier breach. Use percentiles alongside averages.
Exceptions: Offline guard updates require device and receipt timestamps and confidence. Reopened incidents need a defined new response episode. Clock anomalies are flagged.
Acceptance: A labelled timeline yields exact expected durations. Missing milestones produce incomplete metrics. Policy changes do not retrospectively alter signed reports. Pause history remains auditable.
Scope: Includes service measurement. Excludes inferring unrecorded arrival or claiming response guarantees from averages.
Dependencies: P04 status history; F019 dispatch; P09 metrics.
Outputs: Defined durations, service breaches, missing-data flags and policy-versioned reports.

title: Multi site client dashboards
Outcome: Give each customer a permission-limited view of incidents, service delivery, coverage and outstanding work.
Inputs: Authorised sites, reviewed incident data, maintenance status, tasks, service metrics and approved reports.
Configure: Assign customer roles, site scope, permitted details, dashboard widgets and report schedule. Keep operator-only notes hidden by default.
Journey: Client manager signs in and selects an authorised portfolio or site. > Dashboard shows current incidents, coverage and outstanding actions with freshness indicators. > User drills into an allowed incident and sees approved evidence and service history. > User comments or acknowledges an action where permitted. > User exports an approved report; all access follows the same scope rules.
Rules: Tenant isolation applies to widgets, counts, search, exports and links. A zero count with no coverage must not look like a quiet healthy site. Client acknowledgement does not close an operator incident automatically.
Exceptions: Partial site data is labelled. Revoked access invalidates sessions and file requests according to the security policy. Large portfolios require paginated drill-down.
Acceptance: Cross-customer requests fail even with a guessed ID. Stale widgets show update time. Operator-only notes never appear in exports. Portfolio totals disclose excluded or unavailable sites.
Scope: Includes customer service visibility. Excludes unrestricted live camera access by default.
Dependencies: P01 tenancy; P09 reporting; F085 metrics; F081 and F082 health.
Outputs: Customer dashboard, scoped drill-down, actions, approved exports and access audit.

title: People counting and occupancy
Outcome: Estimate entries, exits and occupancy without requiring identity recognition.
Inputs: Directional counts, monitored entrance map, optional in-area estimates and coverage status.
Configure: Select counting method, entrances, initial occupancy, reset policy and reconciliation method. Do not mix incompatible counting methods without an explicit calculation.
Journey: Installer validates every relevant entrance and counting direction. > Administrator establishes the starting occupancy and schedule. > AiWAS records entries and exits and computes the declared estimate. > Analyst reviews trends, drift and missing coverage, then performs authorised reconciliation. > Reports publish counts with methodology and uncertainty.
Rules: Entrance-based occupancy equals starting count plus entries minus exits, subject to known coverage. Negative results flag drift; do not silently clamp without retaining the discrepancy. Reconciliation is a logged adjustment.
Exceptions: Unmonitored exits, groups, children, occlusion and re-entry can affect results. Outages break complete accounting. A site cannot claim exact occupancy from partial coverage.
Acceptance: A staged entrance sequence produces expected directional counts. An outage marks estimates incomplete. Negative drift creates a flag. Manual reset stores reason, actor and prior value.
Scope: Includes anonymous counting. Excludes identity tracking and certified emergency muster accounting.
Dependencies: P02 counting; P07 measurement validation; P09 aggregates.
Outputs: Entries, exits, estimated occupancy, coverage, reconciliation and method version.

title: Queue and waiting time analysis
Outcome: Estimate queue length and waiting times at a defined service point.
Inputs: Queue geometry, person trajectories, service boundary and optional service-start signals.
Configure: Define joining, service-start and abandonment boundaries; set alert thresholds and allowed tracking gaps. State whether wait time is individual observed or aggregate estimated.
Journey: Manager maps the queue and tests representative journeys. > AiWAS measures joining and service events within usable coverage. > Dashboard shows queue length and wait distribution. > A sustained threshold prompts the manager to open another service point or redirect staff. > Completed, abandoned and incomplete journeys are reported separately.
Rules: Do not confuse dwell near the queue with joining. Abandonment is not service completion. Temporary tracking identifiers expire under the counting policy. No face recognition is required.
Exceptions: Families, merged queues, jumping positions and occlusion complicate association. A change in queue layout requires a new geometry version.
Acceptance: A labelled customer journey yields the correct wait interval. Leaving before service records abandonment. Lost tracks remain incomplete. Alerting requires the configured persistence rather than one noisy frame.
Scope: Includes service-flow measurement. Excludes inferring satisfaction, emotion or demographic attributes.
Dependencies: P02 trajectories; P07 queue validation; P09 reporting.
Outputs: Queue estimates, waiting-time distribution, abandonment, coverage and interventions.

title: Movement and dwell analysis
Outcome: Show aggregate use of authorised areas to support layout and operational decisions.
Inputs: Anonymous trajectories, zone definitions, observation windows and privacy-preserving aggregation policy.
Configure: Set analysis zones, time buckets, minimum aggregation group size and retention. Exclude private and out-of-purpose areas.
Journey: Analyst selects a site and approved reporting period. > AiWAS aggregates supported paths and time-in-zone observations. > Dashboard presents heatmaps and dwell distributions with coverage and sample counts. > Analyst compares like-for-like periods and inspects the methodology. > An approved aggregate export supports a layout or staffing decision.
Rules: Heatmaps must disclose whether they show count, duration or normalised activity. Do not expose individual paths in aggregate-only roles. Suppress small groups under the configured privacy threshold. No sensitive-attribute segmentation.
Exceptions: Camera moves, blind areas and changed opening hours can invalidate comparisons. Repeated anonymous sightings are not necessarily unique visitors.
Acceptance: Heatmap totals reconcile with included observations. Small-group suppression applies to exports too. Changed camera layouts are flagged in comparisons. Unique-person counts are not claimed without a validated method.
Scope: Includes aggregate movement analysis. Excludes individual behavioural profiles or demographic targeting.
Dependencies: P09 aggregation; P01 analyst roles; P08 short-lived tracking data.
Outputs: Heatmaps, dwell distributions, methodology, sample counts and coverage disclosures.

title: Resource planning recommendations
Outcome: Recommend patrol timing or staffing scenarios from verified workload and activity, subject to managerial review.
Inputs: Verified incidents, handling time, patrol obligations, activity volumes, staffing constraints and service targets.
Configure: Define planning horizon, minimum contractual coverage, staff availability, skill requirements and cost assumptions. Keep hard constraints separate from optimisation preferences.
Journey: Manager selects sites and a planning period. > AiWAS checks data completeness and builds a baseline workload. > The system presents alternative schedules with assumptions, expected workload and constraint violations. > Manager adjusts assumptions and compares scenarios, then approves a plan for export to the scheduling system. > Actual service results are compared with the approved scenario in a later review.
Rules: Recommendations cannot remove mandatory coverage or publish rosters automatically in initial scope. Historical incidents reflect reporting and coverage bias. Do not score individual staff using inferred traits. Explain the factors behind each recommendation.
Exceptions: Sparse data produces a low-evidence recommendation or no recommendation. Special events and holidays require explicit inputs. Connector failure cannot overwrite the active roster.
Acceptance: Every scenario satisfies declared hard constraints or is visibly invalid. Sparse data is flagged. Approval is required before export. The original roster and approved scenario remain recoverable.
Scope: Includes decision support and scenario planning. Excludes guaranteed loss reduction, autonomous staffing cuts or individual profiling.
Dependencies: F085 timings; F086 portfolio; F087 activity; P06 roster connector.
Outputs: Planning scenarios, assumptions, constraints, manager decision and outcome comparison.
